body:
Implementation parent: [Militia UI rework](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148) · Original planning map: [UI rework decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99) · Authoring task: [Write this area spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/127).

When creating implementation tickets from this spec, follow the [source traceability requirements](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148#source-traceability-and-future-tickets): link back to this spec and carry forward the relevant decision-comment permalinks, amendments, pinned prototypes and capability IDs from the sections below.

## 1. Scope and ownership

Deliver **Event, rollout position 5 of 12**, after [shared Activity slots and action details](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/142), inside the [Week frame](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137) and [campaign navigation shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135). This is the implementation output of [Write the Event implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/127), outside the [UI planning map](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99). Application main inspected: `eef41f7bad19e63ecce858e7a4490c937a4ece89`.

Own Event chance arithmetic, automatic sources, candidate selection, occurrence preparation/tree presentation, every event-specific input, mitigation, reactive Sabotage, check explanations, outcomes and acknowledgements. Preserve all fields supported by the live schemas and rules, including ones absent from the mock. Replace the Event main column only. No new schema, query, mutation argument/result shape, batch endpoint or general adjudication API is approved.

Week frame owns navigation, Phase Readiness aggregation, This phase, reference values, optimistic/save/failure feedback and the next-week transition. [Upkeep](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140) owns the shared dice-total contract already consumed here. Activity owns the source choices/slots and Operating from; Event owns their candidate presentation and Sabotage. [Persistent authoring](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/128) owns carried-event decisions; share the one-event-per-week Overseer allocation and display when Activity/Event already ended a carried event. [Militia corrections](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139) owns source correction/reference-restoration recovery; [Characters & officers](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141) owns its later role/kind/manager migration. Review & confirm owns Confirmation and Table Adjustments. Those later layouts are not prerequisites: keep their existing editors functional.

Implement numbered sections in rules order:

1. **Event chance:** one d100 dice-total field, operating settlement adjustment on that roll, comparison with chance and its breakdown, and result. Name the settlement and link to Activity to change it. Collapse to a truthful one-line explanation when Guarantee Event/Manipulate Events or forced calm makes the chance roll inapplicable; identify the source action/slot. Missing operating-settlement reputation remains an actionable missing input, not a fabricated zero adjustment.
2. **Automatic events:** only when a source is due; show source and count and a stable event block for each required occurrence. These resolve before the normal chance/candidate outcome, including during forced calm.
3. **The event / Event candidates:** event blocks in actual resolution order, with table roll arithmetic, resolved name/status, origin/parent/candidate context, rules text and applicable Twice clause, its own inputs/checks, warnings and Rules Exceptions, outcomes, What happened, and quiet Sabotage. Two candidates are side by side at tablet width; Choose this event identifies the chosen root and the other remains recorded and muted. Preserve independent candidate sets from multiple qualifying Activity choices.
4. **Week outcome:** a short event/uneventful summary only when all required rolls and choices are complete; otherwise expose the missing items through their blocks and the frame. Do not show a final-looking successful outcome for an incomplete attempt.

A step which does not apply becomes one muted explanation. Every block distinguishes Awaiting roll, Happens, Two more, Twice, Reroll, Cannot occur, Sabotaged, Not chosen and no additional effect when appropriate; color alone must not carry the distinction. Render rules text from the existing event/rules sources, not hand-maintained mock calculations.

## 2. Decision sources

Read the full discussions; later approvals override prototype behavior and earlier comments.

- [Event rules-order layout and final branch/reroll amendments](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/108#issuecomment-5837858373): authoritative layout, generic-editor replacement, pre-existing blank occurrences and removal of manual tree buttons. The earlier prototype comment proposing keystroke-created branches is superseded.
- [Shared Event/Persistent Overseer support](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/108#issuecomment-5837427038) and [Persistent rules-order decision](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/109#issuecomment-5837423122), amended by the [final approved shared copy](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/109#issuecomment-5837957108): filled-role toggle and one event per week across both phases, with source names in modifier breakdowns and no holder name or ability in the toggle.
- [Phone and desktop variant B](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/120#issuecomment-5846493929) and [loading, failure, access and maintenance states](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381).
- [Activity decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/106#issuecomment-5835792948), [approved dice totals](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/107#issuecomment-5836751035), and their concrete implementation contracts linked above.
- [Already-shipped settlement chance-roll correction](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/pull/115), Ruleset Version 5; this is not pending work.
- [Twelve-spec rollout and completion gate](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504), `CONTEXT.md`, and the Event phase/action sections in `docs/ai/ironfang-militia/militia-rules.md`, with numeric values/table mapping from `militia-tables.md`.

**Specific source precedence:** the final Event approval states, “A child, an automatic event or a candidate that rolls Roll Twice is rerolled in place.” Apply that restriction to candidate blocks, including a selected top-level Activity candidate. Current main instead allows a selected candidate to expand and represents later/automatic Roll Twice via replacement children. Do not accidentally preserve that expansion because an old test or mock does it. The compatibility and Ruleset Version requirements below cover this approved difference.

## 3. Prototypes

| Reference | Approved variant and route | Pinned commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Event](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/f93ea1cfc7a72b8655e052412008274998779f92), branch `prototype/event` | A, rules order; `/prototype/event?variant=A` | `f93ea1cfc7a72b8655e052412008274998779f92` — review refinements |
| [Responsive shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/de10f4208904ca583d0fbc143bfc6314f0b9c0e7), branch `prototype/responsive-shell` | B; `/prototype/responsive-shell?variant=B`; direct screen `/prototype/responsive-shell/screen?variant=B&phase=event` | `de10f4208904ca583d0fbc143bfc6314f0b9c0e7` |

Keep prototype branches unmerged. Event B–D and responsive A/C are comparison alternatives. Do not ship prototype switches, fixture state, mock reducers or hardcoded example chance/targets. Required differences include Upkeep's shared total fields, complete event details and custom outcomes, compatible legacy trees, source-driven blank allocation, all event types and real save/access/failure states. Use the approved frame's final chrome, not stale captions from a snapshot. Keep theme tokens/fonts and shadcn/ui; thin view components delegate orchestration to focused controllers/service hooks and rules derivation to shared pure utilities.

## 4. Capability accounting

These are planned replacements; the inventory's current-location and current-test columns remain factual until implementation.

| ID | Required replacement and acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| EVT-01 | Chance breakdown, clamping, raw d100 + settlement adjustment versus chance, clear/missing/range behavior; settlement is never applied to table rolls. |
| EVT-02 | Collapsed chance section names each guaranteeing Activity source/slot and links to its existing choice; forced calm has its own explanation. |
| EVT-03 | Required rolled/automatic occurrences already exist with blank dice when needed; automatic source/count is visible. Manual Add rolled/Add automatic controls are replaced, not event capability. |
| EVT-04 | Stable block identity, raw table total, named modifiers, resolved type or Awaiting roll, origin/parent/candidate context and all actual statuses. |
| EVT-05 | Table arithmetic plus + Table modifier; signed value and required reason, edit/remove/clear, preserved provenance and source identity. |
| EVT-06 | Choose this event card; both candidate roots require valid rolls, selection stays tied to owning Activity choice and rejected branch data remains. |
| EVT-07 | Event-specific controls replace the generic structured editor while retaining every schema-supported target/list/officer/check/roll/reward/persistent/Sabotage operation, including nested add/remove and explicit clear. |
| EVT-08 | Attempt it / Let it happen for applicable optional mitigation, per-target where required. Unattempted does not block; attempted missing inputs do. |
| EVT-09 | What happened line with save/edit/clear, correct occurrence subject and existing rules-based requiredness. Preserve independent reaction/persistent acknowledgements. |
| EVT-10 | Dice total + calculated bonus = result versus DC, readable modifier breakdown and per-target check labels. Includes officer and Sabotage checks. |
| EVT-11 | Item-scoped warnings and editable/removable Rules Exception reasons, including nested reward/reaction subjects; frame receives their aggregate. |
| EVT-12 | Complete ordered outcomes: treasury/training/team/reputation/economy changes, queued/persistent effects, narrative benefits and recorded custom outcomes. |
| EVT-13 | One normal Roll Twice expansion; existing blank children, in-place repeated/automatic/candidate rerolls, eligibility replacement, retained hidden children and clear-to-undo. Manual add/remove-tree buttons disappear under the cited approval. |
| EVT-14 | Concrete required inputs per occurrence and aggregate readiness in frame/footer/This phase; inactive branches and optional unattempted checks do not invent blockers. |

Shared IDs and owners:

| ID | Event obligation and owner boundary |
| --- | --- |
| WEEK-02, WEEK-03 | Supply all Event facts without forcing another player's Phase View; Week frame owns navigation/readiness. |
| WEEK-04, WEEK-05, WEEK-06, WEEK-07, WEEK-08, WEEK-10, WEEK-11, WEEK-19 | Use existing shared edits/optimistic preview and frame feedback, rollback/review invalidation, departure protection, Confirmation disabling and successor transition. No local-only saved event data or separate lock. |
| WEEK-12 | Event-shaped body placeholders inside Week frame's loading/failed/no-militia handling. |
| WEEK-13 | Event target/mitigation/candidate cards support touch and keyboard with clear selection; preserve existing shared choice interactions unless their operation is replaced by the approved control. No global choice-card drag removal. |
| WEEK-14, WEEK-15, WEEK-16 | Consume Upkeep's exact dual-form total contract, required/invalid distinction, blank/zero behavior and advisory ranges; Event owns its field/error presentation. |
| WEEK-17 | Own Event block/header/candidate/nesting responsiveness within shell/frame. |
| WEEK-18 | Preserve all Event structured list, discriminated choice, nested roll, custom modifier and Save/Clear operations via specific editors. Upkeep owns roll adapter; other phases retain their own editors. |
| ACT-10, ACT-11, ACT-12, ACT-13, ACT-14, ACT-16, ACT-17, ACT-18 | Activity owns complete source details/cost, modifiers/checks, acknowledgements, warnings/requirements, exceptions and Operating from. Event candidate editing preserves that complete choice and returns upstream missing choices there. Sabotage is Event-reactive, never an Activity deck action. |
| PER-02, PER-03, PER-04, PER-06, PER-07, PER-08, PER-10 | Persistent owns carried-event identity/age, decisions/inputs, table ending, checks/outcomes, warnings/exceptions and preparation. Event preserves nested same-week decisions and shares support allocation/endings; no loss of the existing editor before its successor ships. |
| SUM-02, SUM-06, SUM-07, SUM-08, SUM-09, SUM-10, SUM-11 | Review & confirm owns required-input review, comparison, exceptions, adjustments, warnings, consequences and recorded outcomes; Event supplies accurate occurrence facts/outcomes/reasons and keeps current Summary usable. |
| HIST-05 | Finished weeks owns frozen record presentation; preserve old/new event trees, rolls, versions, acknowledgements and outcome reading now. |
| STATE-01, STATE-02, STATE-03, STATE-05, STATE-06, STATE-07 | Consume shell access/maintenance/failure and frame week states; own Event loading shape and real cross-device/reload persistence. |

No new ID is needed: automatic blank trees and dedicated reactive controls implement EVT-03, EVT-07 and EVT-13. Preserve stable IDs even where controls retire. **Signed-off replacements:** [final Event approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/108#issuecomment-5837858373) removes EVT-03's manual add controls, EVT-13's Add Roll Twice child/Add replacement/Remove Event-and-branches controls, and EVT-07's generic editor shell, replacing their operations as above. EVT-05's accordion moves to arithmetic/+ Table modifier; EVT-08 and EVT-09 become the named controls. WEEK-15's per-die input replacement is Upkeep's approval. No target, raw roll/provenance, acknowledgement, custom outcome, modifier, reaction or Rules Exception is approved for deletion.

## 5. Data, payloads and rules

### Existing edits, blank occurrences and concurrency

Use existing `event_chance`, `event_occurrence`, `event_tree`, owning Activity `detail`, acknowledgement/exception and persistent-decision edits. The existing ordered `eventOccurrenceSchema`/`eventTreeSchema` and candidate collections can hold blank occurrences (no `tableRoll`); parents precede children and IDs remain unique. Requiredness belongs to preparation/Resolution, not rejection of partial drafts. No endpoint/validator extension is needed for this layout.

Implement one pure calculation of the required occurrence positions from current rules facts, then a fill-only preparation operation at the controller/service boundary:

- Required positions are one chance-triggered normal root; each due automatic source's count; two roots per guaranteeing Activity choice; two children of the eligible first normal Roll Twice; and one replacement for an event that cannot occur unless kept with a Rules Exception. Re-evaluate after upstream Activity/outcome changes, not just on visiting Event.
- Reuse existing matching IDs in their saved order. For missing positions derive stable identities scoped to the open draft, owner choice/source, parent and ordinal, with deterministic collision handling. Do not allocate a fresh UUID on every render or remount, use display indices as identity, renumber existing events, or change IDs when a roll changes.
- Submit only when required positions are missing. Normal/automatic topology uses `event_tree`; candidate topology uses the existing owner `detail` with full choice fields retained. Editing an existing roll/detail uses `event_occurrence` and preserves its identity/origin. Ordinary keystrokes in an occurrence's die never create that occurrence or a sibling; required empty fields exist first. Transient unparsed text never changes topology. Parent/chance semantic changes can make pre-existing positions applicable or cause missing blank positions to be prepared.
- Topology preparation is an ordinary saved draft edit, not a hidden synchronous local assumption. While it is pending, show stable blank placeholders and ordinary save feedback; do not send a child edit before its occurrence has been accepted. A failed preparation retains the user's saved data and exposes retry; the phase remains incomplete until required occurrences exist.
- Two devices mounting or observing the same requirement must converge to one set of identities, not duplicate roots/children. Existing `event_tree` conflicts with the whole event tree; candidate `detail` conflicts on its candidates field; an occurrence edit targets the occurrence. On rejection, refresh the accepted observation, retain every other player's value, recompute only missing blanks, and retry that preparation intent with a fresh operation identity. Do not replay an obsolete whole tree, overwrite a remote roll with a blank, or claim unconditional last-writer-wins for rejected stale operations. Transport retries retain their original operation identity. Bound retries and surface ordinary recovery if the conflict persists.
- Existing edits are separate transactions. Do not claim chance + topology, candidate + selection, or moving support across events is one atomic batch. Serialize dependent edits through the existing persistence queue and expose their incomplete intermediate state. Any need for a new argument, result or batch API must return to human approval rather than widening this issue silently.

### Active branches and legacy compatibility

The first eligible **normal** Roll Twice produces exactly two blank children and uses the phase's single expansion. Children, automatic occurrences and Activity candidates with a Roll Twice result say “Roll Twice again: reroll and enter the new die” and reuse their own field. They never create a replacement merely for Roll Twice. “No edit is sent for a second Roll Twice” in the decision means no branch-creation edit; the roll entry and its eventual replacement still use the ordinary existing roll/occurrence edit. A reroll remains required until the replacement value is entered.

An event that cannot occur instead has a nested replacement with blank dice, unless an explicit event-eligibility Rules Exception retains it. Replacement chains for ineligible events remain supported. Resolution order, duplicate Twice dispatch, no-additional-effect clauses and independent duplicate events come from the shared rule engine. Do not conflate a second event of a type with a second Roll Twice result.

Changing a parent away from Roll Twice hides its children from active resolution/readiness; returning it restores their values and identity. Clearing a required die leaves its required occurrence blank. Leaving a chance branch inapplicable, switching candidate or applying forced calm retains recorded input while excluding inactive effects. Never erase a rejected candidate, its nested targets/rewards or its acknowledgements merely because it is muted.

Existing drafts may contain manually assembled branches, surplus roots, historical replacement nodes for repeated Roll Twice, legacy nested support or explicitly stored `eventType`/persistent flags. Opening must not rewrite or migrate these existing values; additive preparation of genuinely missing required blank positions is the separate operation described above. Preserve their data and IDs; render retained values through the same event-specific controls, with a disclosure when currently inactive. Keep root-count/shape inconsistencies visible and repairable through explicit clearing rather than a generic JSON editor. Clearing an extra legacy occurrence's inputs can remove that now-empty surplus position through the existing tree edit; clearing a currently required position retains its blank placeholder. Do not silently pick and apply one of several conflicting roots or discard nonempty branches to obtain readiness.

For old repeated-Roll-Twice replacement chains, show the effective recorded reroll in the parent's visual block while preserving the stored child identity and its complete facts until the player explicitly edits/clears it. Legacy tree interpretation must remain supported in live drafts and record readers; this compatibility does not permit new repeated-Roll-Twice replacement children. Old immutable Resolution Records always render their recorded outcomes/version and are neither rewritten nor re-resolved with today's engine.

### Chance, shared rolls and rules versions

Use the shipped selection calculation: projected notoriety plus uneventful carry based on current rank plus due queued chance modifiers, bounded at 10–95%. Apply the operating settlement reputation to the chance percentile only. Preserve the established strict comparison: below chance triggers, equal/above does not. Show actual raw roll, adjustment, total and threshold separately. Automatic events precede normal handling; forced calm suppresses normal/candidate resolution but does not erase Activity spending or automatic events. Uneventful carry is derived from actual completed outcomes, respecting first-week, automatic/storm, duplicate calm and forced-calm exclusions.

Inherit [Upkeep's exact contract](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140): legacy `{ dice, sides, provenance, modifiers }` or new `{ diceTotal, diceCount, sides, provenance, modifiers }`, strict alternatives, shared normalization. Complete arrays display their sum without read-time rewrites; incomplete/count/sides-mismatched rolls remain incomplete. New edits write totals, keep bonuses separate, preserve provenance/modifiers and natural single-die behavior, and keep out-of-range whole values as advisory. Clearing does not fabricate zero. Cover every nested officer, target, reward/loss and reaction roll, not just d100 fields.

Extra table/check modifiers retain stable source identity, signed value and required reason. Name known contribution sources in the breakdown, not the people supplying them (for example, “Officers +2 · Overseer +3”), following the final approved shared copy. Do not expose raw IDs or count calculated rank/officer/queued/Helpful/Strategist/Overseer bonuses twice. Existing settlement/reputation table-modifier entries are not reactivated by the new UI. Required rolls/DCs/ranges derive from the current rules and event mode, not a hardcoded generic d20.

**Ruleset Version:** the already-shipped reputation correction remains Version 5. Blank allocation, layout and equivalent roll/tree representation alone do not change Weekly Resolution and need no bump. Enforcing the approved candidate Roll Twice restriction changes current selected-candidate behavior: allocate the **next unused Ruleset Version** for that semantic change, coordinate with prior Upkeep and later officer changes, and update client/server resolution together. Do not hardcode 6. Tests must distinguish representation equivalence from that explicit before/after difference. Earlier Resolution Records preserve their original versions and outcomes; no historical rewrite/backfill is included.

### Complete event inputs and outcomes

Use `weekly-draft-facts.ts`, `rules-event-selection.ts`, `rules-event-checks.ts`, event shaping/action/outcome helpers and `event-{facts,checks,messages}.ts[x]` as the live contract. Each event-type panel must cover base, Twice and no-extra/independent modes. This table identifies field coverage, not a substitute rulebook:

| Event family | Event-specific input/outcome coverage |
| --- | --- |
| All Is Calm; Calm before the Storm | Quiet/carry eligibility, forced calm and next-week automatic source/count; no invented acknowledgement or roll requirement. |
| Broke the Code | Item choice, recorded identification/outcome, current-week knowledge benefit and Twice variant. |
| Cache Discovered | Cache choice and loss/retrieval, every cache affected by Twice, independent per-cache Attempt/Let it happen and Secrecy check. |
| Double Agent; Low Morale | Queued versus persistent penalty and action restriction, exact source/age/order, corresponding same-week persistent fields when present. |
| Festival; Market Day | Real operated settlement choice(s), applicable source context, recorded outcome, town-scoped bonus/discount and wider Twice scope. A tracked but unused settlement is not silently treated as operated; existing rule exceptions stay available. |
| Found Fire | Reward list per PC with stable item/recipient identities, name, copper value displayed in gp, decimal weight, alchemical/poison flags and required reward exception; add/edit/remove each reward, including extra rewards for Twice. |
| Hidden Agenda | Retroactive Activity recalculation and any newly required action roll/subject surfaced with a link back to Activity; no invented reward die. |
| High Morale | Ended persistent event identities/order and bonus, including fewer available events than the nominal ending count; reflect endings in Persistent. |
| Invasion | Average Party Level, encounter outcome acknowledgement and derived encounter difficulty; independent repeated occurrences each retain their own facts. |
| Missing in Action; Sickness; Turn Around | Actual team targets, random/GM-selection acknowledgements where required, disabled/missing/lost/queued-return or boosted-team result, conditional checks and ordering. Keep independent duplicate Turn Around behavior and mandatory Sickness Twice save. |
| Night Ops | Recorded narrative outcome and current-week conditional benefit. |
| Raid | Refuge settlement and all person targets, per-person mitigation/check and raw percentile capture roll, lost-refuge/capture outcomes and rescue provenance. No single shared check replaces independent person inputs. |
| Rivalry | Two distinct team targets and acknowledgement, persistent Twice mode and optional officer/social-skill check with character, skill, entered skill bonus and raw roll. |
| Theft | Optional mitigation/check, precise treasury loss, persistent income restriction and interaction with Reduce Danger; preserve differing base/Twice requiredness. |
| Turncoat | Raw loss roll, team selection and acknowledgement for Twice, officer Diplomacy facts/check and unavailable/defection result. |
| War Games; Week of Pain; Week of Serenity | Training/queued-check/loss/gain effects, independent War Games occurrences and explicit no-extra duplicate clauses. |
| Roll Twice | Topology/reroll handling above; no fabricated event outcomes before required leaves resolve. |

Preserve every schema-supported `targets` discriminant (event, item, team, settlement, character, cache); ordered target/check/reward collections; all named `rolls`; officer character/skill/skillBonus/roll; strategist and Overseer selections; stored persistent fields/decisions; and Sabotage identity/team/check/rolls/acknowledgements. Existing values not applicable to the currently resolved type remain visible in retained-input details and intentionally clearable. Do not rebuild an occurrence from only its visible mock fields. Options include entities produced earlier in the same draft, not just saved militia lists; IDs and ownership remain stable.

What happened uses the correct occurrence acknowledgement subject and supports save/edit/clear. Existing engine-required narrative acknowledgements remain required for all relevant types, not just the mock's Invasion; optional notes never become new blockers. Preserve independently scoped nested reaction and persistent-ending acknowledgements. Display recorded custom outcomes and derived changes without treating narrative text as a new numeric adjustment API. Table Adjustments remain in Review & confirm.

Optional mitigation defaults to the existing unattempted interpretation. Attempt it reveals the relevant inputs; Let it happen explicitly records unattempted and does not require a hidden check. For per-target mitigation render independent choices. Support legacy roll-implies-attempted data. Mandatory event checks are never mislabeled optional. Keep errors and Rules Exceptions next to their exact subjects, including rewards and Sabotage, with remove/clear operations intact.

**Sabotage:** the quiet button expands the reaction editor for this selected/eligible event. It selects a Saboteurs team and check kind, enters d20 and notoriety d6 totals, shows DC `15 + rank`, bonuses/result and the occurrence-specific acknowledgement/clear controls. Team availability/use and event selection remain rules-driven/advisory where existing rules allow exceptions; malformed/foreign references remain blocked. Both success and failure add the notoriety roll; success negates the exact occurrence. A failed/incomplete/unselected reaction never silently spends or negates something else. Preserve reactive fields on automatic/replacement events, failures, candidate switches and clear operations. No Activity slot is fabricated.

**Overseer:** show the filled-role support toggle as “Use Overseer support · +3 · one event a week”, substituting the actual contribution, with no holder name or ability. This follows the [final shared copy amendment](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/109#issuecomment-5837957108). Retain the holder identity and ability-derived calculation internally; one chosen event per week is shared across Event and Persistent. A hint names its current event and says tapping moves it. Normalize the displayed selection from existing occurrence/reaction/target/persistent-decision fields without losing legacy facts. Moving support clears conflicting selections in their existing owning records and sets the chosen event using ordinary edits, with pending/error recovery for partial failure; do not pretend this is atomic or silently consume it twice. All checks of that occurrence receive applicable support once. Without a filled role show the truthful unavailable state. Other supported officer/Strategist/custom modifier choices remain available.

## 6. Validation and coverage

Use react-hook-form and zod for event-specific forms with styled field-level errors: required/empty differs from invalid numeric/type/reference input, zero differs from clear, and adjacent controls remain aligned. Rules inconsistencies remain advisory with meaningful Rules Exception reasons where supported; structural invalidity, foreign IDs, illegal tree identities/order and impossible enums stay blocked. Do not use browser-native validation popups. A required-for-resolution field may remain blank in the shared draft. Missing/stale targets stay identifiable and repairable; honor current whole-draft reference validation. Do not promise that clearing one orphan can save while another orphan remains: follow [Militia correction/reference recovery](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139), restore complete source references when necessary, and show ordinary failed-save feedback.

Retain or rewrite with equivalent behavior:

| Existing coverage | Required preservation |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e/canonical-workspace.spec.ts`, `e2e/support/event-workspace.ts` | Shared chance/table rolls, two Roll Twice children, independent player leaf edits, APL, acknowledgement save/clear, zero/blank, reload, stale held edit versus accepted peer edit, navigation while pending, and phone/tablet/desktop controls. Replace add/remove button mechanics with automatic blank fields and clear/hide/restore; do not drop the scenario. |
| `e2e/support/activity-workspace.ts`, `persistent-workspace.ts`, `persistent-qa.ts`, `summary-qa.ts` | Candidate source ownership, reactions/support, Persistent endings/decisions, structured fields, exceptions and final review still work during gradual rollout. |
| `e2e/complete-week.spec.ts`, `existing-militia.spec.ts`, `canonical-cutover.spec.ts`, `access.spec.ts` and nightly flows | Confirmation/reload/history, existing campaign and cross-campaign/access behavior keep equivalent coverage. |
| `e2e/canonical-persistence.spec.ts`, `canonical-confirmation.spec.ts` | Preserve authenticated backend semantic conflict checks, idempotent retries/unknown acknowledgement, rollback, source changes, exact-reviewed-revision Confirmation and successor isolation despite no inventory browser mapping. |
| `event-view.test.tsx` and phase/structured-field tests | Required versus malformed input, zero/clear, nested target percentile defaults/omission, correct occurrence/reaction/persistent acknowledgement subjects, complete Activity candidate ownership and named modifier breakdown. |
| Event selection/action/resource/threat/recurring/acceptance rule suites and weekly draft/persistence/Confirmation suites | Keep every rule case and ordered outcome; update only the explicitly approved reroll semantics and version expectation. |

Add meaningful behavior tests for:

1. Chance minimum/maximum, below/equal/above boundaries, Friendly/Unfriendly on chance only, absent settlement versus unknown reference, carry/queued effects and forced calm with automatic events. Table modifier signed values/reasons/removal must not reapply settlement reputation.
2. Concurrent initial blank allocation and refresh/remount do not duplicate or erase events; unrelated remote occurrence values survive. Dropped acknowledgement/retry and competing topology/detail edits yield one accepted structure. Pending initialization prevents edits against absent IDs; changing the source while preparation is queued never creates stale candidates or writes into a successor draft.
3. First normal Roll Twice creates exactly two blank fields before entry; clearing/hiding/restoring preserves identities and recorded child facts. Additional child/automatic/candidate Roll Twice rerolls in its own field with no new descendants. **Before/after regression:** a selected Activity candidate with Roll Twice currently expands; under the approved version it requires an in-place reroll. Another unselected candidate with Roll Twice also remains incomplete until rerolled; automatic rerolls do not spend the normal expansion. Cover ineligible replacement chains and Rules Exceptions separately.
4. Existing replacement-chain drafts and records remain readable with their independent targets/rolls/outcomes; legacy inactive/surplus data remains visible and explicitly repairable. No read-time rewrites of existing legacy facts, silent loss, hidden blocker or new blank branch in history; required additive live preparation remains allowed as specified above. Two candidate sources remain independent and selection is never retargeted by move/swap/replace/clear of a source choice.
5. Every event type/mode above has a reachable field and outcome path, especially Raid per-person dice, Cache Discovered multiple targets, Found Fire rewards/classification exceptions, skill bonus zero/negative, required narrative outcomes beyond Invasion, nested persistent-ending and reaction notes, and targets/items produced earlier in the draft. Hidden Agenda can expose upstream requirements without inventing values.
6. Base/Twice/independent/no-extra dispatch and dynamic replacement ordering; optional no-attempt versus incomplete attempted mitigation; required Sickness/Turncoat checks; successful/failed/unavailable/incomplete Sabotage, notoriety both ways and exact-event negation. Support moved between Event/Persistent and legacy nested selections cannot duplicate its use; failure between edits stays visible and recoverable.
7. Old-array/new-total mixed rolls across all nested fields yield equivalent calculation, modifiers/provenance/natural results and range warnings. Legacy partial/wrong-spec rolls stay incomplete. Frozen old/new records retain source/outcome/version equality after visits.
8. Two organization members can edit every allowed Event input with immediate preview and saved/failed/remote feedback; no GM-only controls, claims or locks. Foreign campaign/draft/team/person/item/cache/settlement/event/parent/choice IDs are refused on the server; event content does not render outside the shell access gate. Confirmation disables every input, and later receipts cannot affect the next draft.

Use real touch/keyboard/browser checks for card selection, ordinary page scrolling begun on a card, nested fields, candidate selection and sheets/disclosures. Focus and names identify event/target/roll even when a sibling disappears; announce saving/failure/missing inputs without color dependence. Do not hide errors behind an inactive sheet or fixed bars. Run `pnpm -s typecheck`, `pnpm -s lint` and relevant component/rules/Convex/browser tests; report actual commands/results, not an inferred pass from a test file's existence.

## 7. Routes and rollout

Render at `/campaigns/<id>/week?phase=event`. Shell redirects `/canonical-workspace?campaign=<id>&phase=event` with campaign/phase retained; direct entry, reload, Back/Forward and Activity links keep context. Selection of a Phase View, input disclosure or reaction panel is local UI; the event/candidate decisions and roll values are shared. No persisted panel-selection state or extra endpoint is needed.

Shipping dependency: Navigation shell → Week frame → Upkeep → Activity → **Event** → Persistent → Review & confirm → Setup → Militia corrections → Characters & officers → Finished weeks → campaign home. Use native implementation dependencies, independently of the authoring graph. Keep old Persistent/Summary/history and correction/roster editors reachable and compatible until their replacements ship. Remove the old Event generic form/tree controls only after all existing field operations and legacy repair are reachable through the replacement and regression coverage passes.

Tablet landscape (reference about 1180×820): numbered main-column sections, candidate pairs, nested event blocks within the settled stepper/reference/footer frame. Phone 390×844 and landscape: section effect text wraps, roll labels take a full row, candidates stack, nesting uses smaller indentation and target/reward/check fields wrap without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs/disclosures remain above the keyboard, safe-area inset, status strip and bottom tabs. Desktop ≥1280 (test 1440×900): body scrolls in the frame's middle column, rail left/reference right, footer beneath middle; no second page scroll region or clipped nested controls.

During loading show Event-shaped block/roll placeholders within the frame; accessible loading text stays. Failure/retry, no militia, unavailable campaign, signed-out and maintenance follow shell/frame owners. A valid quiet week is a collapsed explanation and eventual outcome, not an empty/error page. Missing teams, settlements, items or officers show actionable truthful selection states; preserve recorded missing references rather than silently selecting another target. Maintenance stays readable, with ordinary failed-write feedback. The frame owns the confirmed-week notice and transition on every device.

### Published implementation handoffs

Implement after [Implement shared Activity slots and action details](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/142). The next shipping area is [Implement carried Persistent events and shared support decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/144). The native dependencies between implementation issues encode this shipping order; authoring tasks are already complete.

## 8. Shippable when

- EVT-01–14 and every listed shared obligation have reachable equivalents. Only cited control/chrome replacements are retired; no hidden event type, nested target/reward/check, custom outcome or legacy repair is lost.
- Required blank occurrences converge across devices through existing semantic edits, inactive branches preserve their data, candidate ownership stays intact, and clearing/rerolls never depend on child-creation keystrokes or an unapproved API.
- Chance arithmetic uses the already-shipped reputation fix; the approved candidate reroll behavior has a focused regression and next-unused Ruleset Version with equal client/server behavior. Old records remain immutable and readable.
- Optional mitigation, mandatory checks, exact-event Sabotage, one-event Overseer allocation, ordered outcomes and upstream/downstream handoffs work with real draft data and both roll representations.
- Approved tablet/phone/desktop layouts and access/loading/failure/empty/maintenance/Confirmation states are usable by touch, keyboard and assistive technology. Shared edits, rejection/recovery, reload and successor isolation pass.
- Update `docs/ui-capability-inventory.md` with actual implementation locations and retained/new coverage, preserving IDs and the removal sources. Required checks and relevant browser/backend tests pass. No prototype merge, unapproved payload change or lost capability.
