body:
Implementation parent: [Militia UI rework](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148) · Original planning map: [UI rework decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99) · Authoring task: [Write this area spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/130).

When creating implementation tickets from this spec, follow the [source traceability requirements](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148#source-traceability-and-future-tickets): link back to this spec and carry forward the relevant decision-comment permalinks, amendments, pinned prototypes and capability IDs from the sections below.

## 1. Scope and ownership

Deliver guided **Militia Setup** at `/campaigns/<id>/setup`, for both a new militia and an existing campaign's current table state. This is shipping area **8 of 12**, after Review & confirm and before Militia corrections. This issue implements the approved design; its authoring task is [Write the Setup implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/130) in [Rework the militia UI for ease of use](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99).

Own the nine steps, free navigation and status, browser-resumed unfinished input, inline Add character, defaults, structural validation, section warnings, review/start, initialization feedback, live setup collision and already-started page. Establish reusable section editors and client validation/warning routing consumed by Militia corrections. Setup initializes facts and an ordinary Weekly Draft; it neither resolves a week nor starts a separate gameplay model.

The [Navigation shell implementation](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135) owns routes, campaign access, organization/account controls, the maintenance banner and shared failed-load component. Setup owns its skeleton and failure content inside that shell. Week frame owns Phase View eligibility, setup-note display and shared weekly editing after entry. Militia corrections owns section merging, correction reasons/conflicts and draft-reference warnings; Characters & officers owns later kind/Hit Dice/manager-rule changes and migration of every Setup consumer. No correction-history feature, shared setup draft, new authorization role or character builder is included.

## 2. Decision sources

The full discussions and amendments in these decisions govern implementation:

- [Separate guided Setup from Militia Correction](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/103#issuecomment-5834024251): nine steps, free navigation, local resume, inline character creation, validation and reuse boundaries.
- [Approve index/detail Setup, without explanatory captions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5844235691): variant B, statuses, review, footer and explicit caption removals.
- [Approve shared loading, failed and started-militia states](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381): **initially started Setup is a page with links, superseding the earlier automatic redirect on initial visit**. The live false→true transition while an unfinished form is open still follows the earlier automatic redirect decision.
- [Approve stacked responsive pages](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/121#issuecomment-5846528685): variant C for phone and desktop; [responsive shell approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/120#issuecomment-5846493929) owns the surrounding bottom tabs/More.
- [Approve officer behavior and kind/Hit Dice changes](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/112#issuecomment-5836835106) and [approve character-record kind ownership](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/114#issuecomment-5844673552): later Characters & officers migration, including Setup compatibility. The latter supersedes the setup-correction prototype's separate character-page layout.
- [Approve twelve-area rollout and ownership](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504): Setup ships with current character CRUD before that migration; later owner updates already-shipped consumers. Its next-unused-Ruleset-Version instruction supersedes the older literal version number.

Implementation must add the agreed missing `CONTEXT.md` glossary entry: **Militia Setup** is the one-time recording of a militia's current table state, including a mid-campaign starting point, that opens its first Weekly Draft without resolving that week. Keep the entry domain-focused; user-facing terms are **Set up militia** and **Start militia week**, not ledger or internal identifiers. Militia Correction and Officer glossary additions belong to their respective later owners.

## 3. Prototypes

| Prototype | Approved selection | Pinned source | Application |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prototype/setup-correction` | B, index and detail; `/prototype/setup-correction?variant=B` (Setup screen) | [`c479521ba1cfb2e7ee931fa5b9daf4254280e8a9`](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/c479521ba1cfb2e7ee931fa5b9daf4254280e8a9) | Tablet landscape, nine-step index, one detail pane, statuses and footer. |
| `prototype/responsive-pages` | C, Stacked; `/prototype/responsive-pages?variant=C`, choose Setup in the prototype state panel | [`cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c`](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c) | Phone accordion rows; desktop wider index, preview lines and centred two-pane layout; page-state frames. |

Prototype branches stay unmerged. Port the design using real shadcn/ui components, existing theme tokens/fonts and production controllers, without mock records, variant toggles or yellow state controls. Later state/caption approvals override stale mock behavior. The mock PC/NPC toggle and commandant level fallback cannot migrate the backend ahead of the owning Characters & officers implementation; preserve today's representable kinds and required facts until then.

**Concrete layout and flow:** Starting point New/Existing sits above the numbered index. Tablet shows one step in the right pane; each index entry has a status icon and text such as “2 to fix”, “1 warning”, or “Optional · skipped”. Review & start is separated by a rule. Errors take precedence over warnings, then completion; status must not rely on color alone. Free step jumps and Next never submit or prevent leaving an incomplete step. New mode marks Character conditions, Assets and Carried effects optional, initially empty; skipping never clears entered values. Review includes setup notes, warnings grouped by step with links, and the blocking error summary after a start attempt. The sticky tablet footer offers **Next: <step name>**, then **Start militia week** only on Review.

Below 768px, show one scrolling list of all nine step rows, one expanded at a time, with New/Existing above it. Status captions remain visible and Next is inside the expanded row. Opening a summary link expands the correct row and focuses its field. From 1280px, retain two panes, widen the index with previews from entered values and centre the page at a maximum width. Tablet landscape is the primary target. Preserve form state and focus across breakpoint changes; render one logical form, not duplicate mounted editors. Buttons, status text and error links remain keyboard and screen-reader usable. Long names, nested repeatable entries and errors wrap without horizontal page overflow or row misalignment; all controls stay above or scroll clear of the shell's fixed phone tabs.

## 4. Capability accounting

The inventory's existing rows remain the current-state baseline until implementation ships. The following is **planned ownership and coverage**, with exact stable IDs; omission from simplified prototype data is not approval to remove a field.

| ID | Destination and acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| SETUP-01 | Starting point: New/Existing retains entered facts; New defaults rank 1, training 0, 1,000 copper (10 gp). Switching Existing clears the first-militia-week skip as today. |
| SETUP-02 | Starting point: focus, rank, training, treasury in copper and notoriety, with current numeric semantics and defaults. |
| SETUP-03 | Week: current week, start day, first militia week shown only for New, previous week uneventful and optional last persistent buyoff week. |
| SETUP-04 | Week: all five open phases; Persistent without carried events warns and opens Upkeep under current eligibility rules. |
| SETUP-05 | People & officers: campaign records, roster inclusion/removal, current kind, Hit Dice and six officer-role toggles. Removing a person clears its roles and managers; do not delete the character record. Keep all current kinds/Hit Dice validation until the named migration. |
| SETUP-06 | Teams: add/remove, name, type, active/disabled/missing condition, reward-limit exemption, manager from roster and notes. |
| SETUP-07 | Character conditions: add/remove, character, available/hidden/captured/recovering/dead, headquarters/refuge/elsewhere location and description, PCs must rescue, capture source/week, rescued/restored weeks. |
| SETUP-08 | Settlements: add/remove, name, reputation, secured/occupied, temporary reputation shift, Reduce Danger shift/end week and refuge activated/end weeks. |
| SETUP-09 | Carried effects: persistent-event instances with type, started week, processing order, all supported entity targets and Theft mitigation week. Repeated types retain separate identities and targeting. |
| SETUP-10 | Assets: items, including add/remove, name, value, militia/character ownership, identified, weight and location. |
| SETUP-11 | Assets: caches, including location, class, status, secure/extradimensional, return Activity week and item contents. |
| SETUP-12 | Assets: orders, including item, delivery settlement, source/kind, ordered week/day, due day/Activity week, price, delivery days, enchantment value and receipt recorded/cleared with received day. Preserve decimal enchantment input. |
| SETUP-13 | Assets: marketplaces, including source, settlement, available/expires week, availability, availability percentage, sale percentage and contraband. |
| SETUP-14 | Carried effects: queued effects with source, start/end week and every existing branch: check modifier, upkeep loss multiplier, activity training multiplier, event chance, all is calm, automatic events, blocked action, team unavailable, team return and narrative. Retain each branch's fields. |
| SETUP-15 | Carried effects: one-use bonuses with source, applies-to, team, phase, amount and available/consumed week. |
| SETUP-16 | Carried effects: skill benefits with characters, skills, bonus type/value, settlement, after-dark and start/end week. |
| SETUP-17 | Carried effects: Market Day benefits with settlements and start/end week. |
| SETUP-18 | Review & start: optional setup notes, persisted unchanged and displayed after entry through Week frame's WEEK-09. |
| SETUP-19 | Live non-blocking section warnings and collected review warnings with links; remove only the approved keep-and-explain hint. |
| SETUP-20 | Field errors for empty versus malformed values and linked review error summary; preserve structural/reference validation. |
| SETUP-21 | Start militia week, Starting militia… pending feedback, retry with values retained on failure; no duplicate initialization. |
| SETUP-22 | Initially started: “This militia is already set up.” with Open week N and Open militia, inside the shell. |
| SETUP-23 | Setup-specific responsive skeleton and screen-reader loading status, failed-load card/Try again; shell handles unavailable/signed-out campaigns. |
| SETUP-24 (new) | Browser resume of unfinished values, including incomplete numeric input, nested entries, selected step and mode, safely scoped to the signed-in account, organization and campaign. |
| SETUP-25 (new) | Nine freely navigable steps, live status/counts, optional grouping, Next and linked review navigation across all breakpoints. |
| SETUP-26 (new) | Inline Add character creates through existing character dialog/mutation and appears reactively in People & officers without losing unfinished setup. |
| SETUP-27 (new) | Another player completes setup while the form is open: detect started transition and automatically open the current week without overwriting the accepted setup. |

Shared IDs and owners:

| ID | Setup obligation and other owner |
| --- | --- |
| NAV-11 | Consume shell's same-campaign Setup entry from Week/Militia; Week frame/Militia corrections own their empty-page links. |
| NAV-13 | Own both started-page links; Navigation shell supplies scoped destinations. |
| NAV-14 | Own successful start navigation to the same campaign's requested eligible phase; shell routes it, Week frame enforces Phase View eligibility. |
| NAV-15 | Preserve all phase values/fallback; shell owns parsing and Week frame owns later phase navigation. |
| NAV-17 | Consume shell's scoped route and legacy redirect contract; preserve setup bookmarks. |
| CHAR-03 | Reuse existing full Add character dialog: name, current kind, level, six ability scores, notes and validation; Characters & officers owns overall CRUD and its later redesign. |
| CHAR-07 | Inline character failure keeps its form values with existing error presentation; Characters & officers owns general CRUD errors. |
| CHAR-08 | Newly created/changed character options arrive on other members' devices; Characters & officers owns records' realtime contract. |
| LEDG-02 | Shared Values editor/validation primitives; Militia corrections owns correction UI and save behavior. |
| LEDG-03 | Shared roster/officer/team-manager field primitives; Militia corrections retains the legacy roster/officer editor until Characters & officers replaces it. |
| LEDG-04 | Shared section field primitives and reference semantics; Militia corrections owns all correction entry points. |
| LEDG-07 | Shared section-keyed warning presentation; Militia corrections owns warning aggregation at each correction save. |
| WEEK-09 | Persist notes; Week frame owns their display during normal play. |
| STATE-01 | Render under shell maintenance banner; inputs stay readable/editable and server pause failures use ordinary save feedback. |
| STATE-02 | Own Setup layout skeleton; shell owns name/account loading. |
| STATE-03 | Supply “Militia setup could not be loaded.” and page-local Try again using shell's failed-load card. |
| STATE-04 | Respect shell's organization selection and unavailable state; never restore another organization's setup into this page. |
| STATE-05 | Own Setup-specific loading/failure/started state while shell owns campaign access. |
| STATE-06 | Setup accepted state/characters persist and are shared; unfinished form is deliberately browser-local. |
| STATE-07 | Consume shell's neutral sign-in/unavailable campaign gate before rendering protected data or restoring its form. |

**Signed-off removals/replacements:** [prototype approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5844235691) removes explanatory captions, including the browser-persistence note, People introduction and SETUP-19 keep-and-explain hint; it does not remove persistence, warnings, field labels, required validation or status captions. [Shared-state approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381) replaces SETUP-22's old completion text and initial-entry redirect with the two-link started page, and SETUP-23's visible loading paragraph with a layout skeleton plus accessible status. No data-entry capability is removed.

## 5. Data, payloads and rules

**No backend schema, query/mutation argument or result-shape change; no Weekly Resolution change, Ruleset Version bump or database migration in this issue.** Reuse `canonicalSetup.options({ campaignId })`, `canonicalSetup.initialize({ campaignId, initializationId, setup })`, the existing `MilitiaSetup` schema, `newMilitiaSetup` and `prepareMilitiaSetup`. Member authorization and campaign-scoped references remain server-enforced. Setup choices remain personal until initialization; no shared setup persistence or locks are added. Inline character creation is already shared immediately and is independent of starting the militia.

Read the current seams before implementation: `src/components/militia-setup/{screen,form,fields,roster,world,effects,assets,carry}.tsx`, `src/lib/canonical-setup.ts`, `canonical-roster.ts`, `canonical-weekly-source.ts`, `weekly-draft-references.ts`, `src/components/character-manager.tsx`, its form/types, `sharedQueries.ts`, and `convex/canonicalSetup.ts`. Read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` before backend-related work. Keep routes thin, use focused form/controller and mutation hooks, and keep defaults/rules/warning derivation pure; effects are for external persistence/subscription boundaries, not duplicated derived state.

**Shared editor contract:** one typed form model retains all values while steps unmount. Split the present composite editors only as needed to expose the nine step boundaries (for example People versus Teams, Settlements versus persistent events, conditions versus benefits). Editors bind existing field paths, use shared field controls, accept authorized character choices, and do not perform backend saves. Share field-level and cross-reference validators with correction consumers. Create client warning descriptors with stable section keys/message/optional field target for Starting point, Week, People & officers, Teams, Settlements, Character conditions, Assets and Carried effects; correction callers can additionally select asset/benefit subsections. Preserve the existing `prepareMilitiaSetup(...).warnings` string/result contract and backend responses; enrich or derive section metadata locally without introducing a wire field or classifying English strings by fragile substring matching. Map root/cross-section reference errors to their relevant section and retain a visible summary fallback. Militia corrections later owns latest-snapshot merging and conflicts; its existing full correction form remains usable through this refactor.

**Validation:** react-hook-form + zod, `noValidate`, styled field messages and links. All steps are freely reachable; only Start is blocked by invalid data. Distinguish required/empty from invalid type/format, preserve valid decimals where supported, stable entity IDs/order and current hard reference checks (missing carried-event targets, incomplete order delivery facts, foreign records, impossible enum/ID types). Rules mismatches such as rank/training, caps, notoriety and manager limits stay advisory with values preserved; no acknowledgment box or extra required notes. Use existing deterministic defaults from rules utilities, never overwrite an intentional edit when navigating or changing mode. Do not silently relax required current commandant facts before the named migration.

**Browser resume:** persist a versioned client form envelope scoped by account/organization/campaign, including raw editable values and initialization identity; validate the envelope separately from submit validity so “invalid” and empty numeric edits survive reload for repair. Restore only after authorized campaign/options resolve and before writing defaults. Navigation away/back or reloading preserves unfinished input. Invalid/corrupt envelopes cannot crash the page, be auto-submitted or leak into another campaign; storage unavailable must not prevent entering or starting setup, and a persistence failure gets concise outcome-oriented feedback. Do not clobber active inputs on options refresh. Once setup is authoritatively started, retire its unfinished envelope; later visits must not resurrect it. No autosave to Convex or cross-device form mirroring.

**Start/race state machine:** resolve first authoritative options result before deciding entry state. If it is already started, render the two-link page, even when a stale local envelope exists. Obtain N from an existing authorized current-week read (`canonicalDraftPersistence.workspace` via the established campaign context); `options` currently has no week field, so do not extend its result for the label. If options was unstarted and the form is open, a subsequent started transition navigates automatically to that campaign's current week. On this player's successful submission, preserve the requested eligible phase rather than letting a racing options update redirect to Upkeep first. An external winner opens its accepted current week with the usual default Phase View. Initialization retries preserve the same attempt ID and submitted source; retain the server's same-ID/same-source idempotence and changed-source/competing-request rejection. Disable duplicate submissions while pending; an unknown acknowledgment cannot justify submitting a different source under an already-accepted identity. Failure retains fields and normal retry feedback; authoritative started state wins over a transient error. Starting never overwrites another player's accepted militia or advances the week.

**Character creation and later migration:** reuse/extract the existing dialog/form and `character.createCharacter`; preserve all fields/errors and let `options.characters` deliver the created record. Creating a record does not automatically assign roles or a manager; roster inclusion remains explicit. Refresh available records without wiping local choices; current stale-reviewed-character rejection remains safe and recoverable. This shipping stage retains character-record `pc | officer_npc`, roster `pc | officer_npc | other_npc` and required commandant Hit Dice. The later Characters & officers implementation must update Setup's schema/validation, roster kinds mirrored from authoritative character records, any character-option data source (current options omits kind), inline dialog, manager warnings/calculations, optional Hit Dice with level fallback, current drafts and persisted browser envelopes. Dropping roster kind is not approved. That later owner allocates the next unused Ruleset Version for changed resolution behavior and preserves older Resolution Records; Setup must not pre-apply the prototype's incompatible enum or fallback.

## 6. Validation and coverage

Keep equivalent coverage for **every existing `e2e/` scenario**, including direct persistence/Confirmation contracts, even when locators change. Navigate to relevant steps before filling controls; do not skip prior field assertions because editors now collapse.

| Existing coverage | Required equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `existing-militia.spec.ts`; `canonical-workspace.spec.ts` through `support/setup-workspace.ts` | New and mid-campaign entry, 1,000-copper default, existing week/start day, advisory notoriety, invalid numeric rejection, people/teams/conditions/settlements/Reduce Danger/one-use/Market Day carry, notes, selected Event entry versus another player's Upkeep, ordinary Upkeep and Confirmation/next week, outsider rejection and viewport bounds. |
| `character-ledger.spec.ts`, `access.spec.ts`, `support/nightly-flows.ts` | Full character creation/validation/edit/reload, shared records and officer corrections remain accessible, including before setup; preserve organization/member isolation. |
| `realtime-action-slot.spec.ts`, `complete-week.spec.ts`, `canonical-cutover.spec.ts` | Started militia enters the same shared Action Slots/Confirmation lifecycle; accepted source survives reload and historical results remain intact. |
| `canonical-persistence.spec.ts`, `canonical-confirmation.spec.ts`, remaining workspace phase scenarios | Keep required real-auth/isolation, competing writers, stale review, delayed/dropped acknowledgments, rollback, immutable history and ordinary phase-edit coverage. Setup refactors cannot weaken these gates. |
| `src/lib/canonical-setup.test.ts`; `src/components/militia-setup/form.test.tsx` | Defaults, advisory rank cap, existing-mode first-week skip, empty/malformed numbers, carried conditions/benefits, order decimal/receipt fields, repeated-event identity/targets/order and missing-reference blocking; correction reason remains required. |
| `convex/canonicalSetup.integration.test.ts` | Lifecycle/idempotent retry, complete import, ordinary-member authority versus outsider, first-use mid-campaign Confirmation, atomic foreign-reference rejection, competing initialization, no-militia campaign and existing first-week-skip normalization. |

Add meaningful tests for free navigation with invalid input, preserved repeatable entries between steps/breakpoints, optional steps with entered values, linked summary focus and warning grouping. Test browser reload/leave-return, scoped isolation, malformed/unavailable storage, setup completion clearing, and stale envelope not replacing server state. Test inline Add character failure and reactive success in two members' contexts while all unrelated local fields remain intact.

Exercise two simultaneous setup forms: each has independent unfinished input; one starts; the other automatically opens the accepted week; only one initialized source/draft exists. Separately test a fresh or bookmarked `/setup` visit to an already-started militia stays on the started page with both working links, and own successful submission preserves a requested eligible phase despite options timing. Check rejected/unknown-ack retries retain existing idempotence, and missing Persistent eligibility falls back as before. Cover loading, failure/Try again, no access, wrong organization, sign-out and maintenance during entry and submission; campaign switches must not retarget a delayed write or expose old form data. Verify phone/tablet/desktop and keyboard/screen-reader behavior, including long dynamic rows, errors and the inline dialog.

Run `pnpm -s typecheck`, `pnpm -s lint`, relevant unit/component/Convex integration tests and affected required/nightly E2E journeys using the repo's existing isolated-preview harness. Preserve auth and required-result gates; report actual execution and live-service limitations, not unrun checks as passes. This planning task does not deploy or run the application.

## 7. Routes and rollout

Use `/campaigns/<id>/setup`; shell's `/canonical-setup?campaign=<id>` redirect preserves the campaign and reaches the new page. A missing campaign follows the shell fallback to `/campaigns`. A started bookmark remains at Setup until a link is chosen; only a successful start or live transition redirects. Open militia targets `/campaigns/<id>/militia`, and Open week N targets that campaign's current week. Keep normal shell navigation and all sections available.

Native implementation chain: **Review & confirm → this Setup issue → Militia corrections → Characters & officers**, within the complete twelve-area order. [Write the Review & confirm implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/129), [Write the Militia corrections implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/131), and [Write the Characters & officers implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/132) identify output owners until their implementation issues exist; replace/add output links and native edges as they publish. Authoring dependencies are not shipping dependencies. The navigation contract already exists in [Implement the campaign navigation shell and scoped routes](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135).

Until this ships, keep existing Setup hosted in the shell. Remove its single long-form presentation only after all nine-step capabilities are reachable. Keep the current correction form and record CRUD functional throughout shared-editor extraction; their later replacements ship separately. Militia corrections may reuse these primitives but must retain its roster/officer fallback until Characters & officers delivers equivalent operations. The later kind/rules migration owns backward compatibility for Setup already in use, including browser resume, rather than forcing this issue to wait for that later UI.

### Published implementation handoffs

Implement after [Implement Review & confirm with ordered consequences and exact reviewed Confirmation](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/145). The next shipping area is [Implement in-place Militia corrections and reference repair](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139). The native dependencies between implementation issues encode this shipping order; authoring tasks are already complete.

Other referenced implementation contracts: [Implement Characters & officers with role corrections and compatible kind migration](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141).

## 8. Shippable when

- All nine steps preserve every listed field/action, defaults, optional states and freely navigable statuses; start blocks only current structural/integrity errors and presents advisory warnings clearly. Review links reach/focus the correct editor at every breakpoint.
- Unfinished input survives navigation/reload within its account/organization/campaign. Shared character creation appears reactively, without converting unfinished Setup into a shared draft or losing entries.
- First entry to an already-started militia shows the two-link page; a live competing completion redirects; own initialization opens the requested eligible phase exactly once. Stale browser values never overwrite an accepted setup.
- Tablet index/detail, phone single-open rows with inline Next and desktop wider index/previews all work with complete keyboard access, readable states and no obscured controls.
- The existing correction editor still works after shared section/validation extraction. All migration touchpoints and adjacent ownership are linked; no unapproved payload/rules changes or removed fields occur.
- Militia Setup's glossary entry is added, inventory current locations/coverage are updated only for what shipped, and the specified typecheck, lint and relevant tests pass with affected live journey evidence recorded. Prototype branches remain unmerged.

body:
Implementation parent: [Militia UI rework](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148) · Original planning map: [UI rework decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99) · Authoring task: [Write this area spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/131).

When creating implementation tickets from this spec, follow the [source traceability requirements](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148#source-traceability-and-future-tickets): link back to this spec and carry forward the relevant decision-comment permalinks, amendments, pinned prototypes and capability IDs from the sections below.

## 1. Scope and ownership

Deliver **Militia Correction** in place at `/campaigns/<id>/militia`: browse current militia facts by section, correct one section at a time with a required reason, preserve other players' changes, and keep affected weekly choices repairable. This is shipping area **9 of 12**, after [guided Militia Setup](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138) and before Characters & officers. Authoring comes from [Write the Militia corrections implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/131) in [Rework the militia UI for ease of use](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99); this implementation issue is outside that planning map.

Own Values, Teams and their managers, Settlements, Character conditions, Items, Caches, Orders, Marketplaces, Carried benefits, and the read-only Week & carried effects view. Own section merges/conflicts, validation/warnings, correction feedback and the correction-to-week reference-repair handoff. Reuse Setup's section editors and client warning descriptors. Keep the current roster/officer editor reachable until Characters & officers supplies its replacement; the temporary fallback and section editor are mutually exclusive on this page. Character record CRUD remains reachable on Characters & officers, including before setup.

[Navigation shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135) owns campaign access, scoped routes, organization/account controls, maintenance banner and shared failure component. [Week frame](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137) and phase owners retain weekly editing, reference readiness, save feedback and Confirmation. This issue supplies the missing correction/recovery integration where those earlier pages need it. Later Characters & officers owns `pc | npc`, mirrored roster kind, role-dependent manager rules, Hit Dice fallback and migration of all consumers, including this page. No correction-history display/query, Historical Correction, new authority role, new weekly action, or backend contract change belongs here.

## 2. Decision sources

Read full discussions and amendments, with later approvals taking precedence:

- [Separate Militia Setup and Militia Correction](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/103#issuecomment-5834024251): section boundary, required free-text reasons, latest-snapshot merge, same-section conflict, read-only carry and known whole-draft reference validation limitation.
- [Approve Militia index/detail and remove explanatory captions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5844235691), including the [team-removal handoff from Upkeep](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5836758014).
- [Approve the officer board and separate roster/officer corrections](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/114#issuecomment-5844673552): permanent roster/officer ownership is Characters & officers; managers stay with Teams. This supersedes the earlier character strip/side-sheet prototype. Its quick-pick reasons apply to that page, not to Militia's explicitly free-text-only reasons.
- [Approve shared loading, failure, no-militia and maintenance states](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381).
- [Approve stacked responsive pages](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/121#issuecomment-5846528685), inside the [responsive shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/120#issuecomment-5846493929).
- [Approve twelve-area rollout, payload ownership and completion gate](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504): retain roster/officer fallback; explicitly cover orphan repair without silently broadening the backend.

Add the agreed missing glossary entry to `CONTEXT.md` during implementation: **Militia Correction** is a reasoned change to the militia's current recorded facts outside Weekly Resolution, preserving the current week and its prepared choices; affected choices must be reviewed before Confirmation. Distinguish it from Historical Correction, which rewrites a finished week. Use **Militia**, **Correct <section>**, **Reason for correction**, and **Save correction** in the product, never “ledger”, internal identifiers or revision jargon.

## 3. Prototypes

| Branch | Approved route/variant | Pinned commit | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prototype/setup-correction` | `/prototype/setup-correction?variant=B&screen=militia` — B, index and detail | [`c479521ba1cfb2e7ee931fa5b9daf4254280e8a9`](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/c479521ba1cfb2e7ee931fa5b9daf4254280e8a9) | Tablet Militia sections, warnings, correction pane, conflict and read-only carry. |
| `prototype/responsive-pages` | `/prototype/responsive-pages?variant=C`; choose Militia in the state panel — C, Stacked | [`cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c`](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c) | Phone accordion sections, desktop wider index/previews/centred page, responsive page-state frames. |

Leave branches unmerged. Use production shadcn/ui, theme tokens/fonts and controllers; omit mock data, variant/state controls and captions removed by approval. The prototype's character screen and simplified conflict/reference simulation are not backend authority. Implement the later states and real repair contracts below.

Tablet landscape: list nine correctable sections at left, each with an appropriate value/count and warning icon; below them put **Week & carried effects** in **Changes through the week**. The selected pane shows readable facts, warnings and **Correct <section>**. Correct replaces its contents with fields, warnings, **This affects the open week**, reason and Save/Cancel. Other section selectors are disabled while editing, including the temporary roster/officer fallback. Cancel drops only this local correction and shows the latest accepted facts. There is one local correction on a device, not a cross-device claim or lock.

Below 768px, the index and detail become one scrolling list, one expanded row at a time. Correct edits inside that row; other rows are disabled until Save/Cancel. The correction reason/actions bar sits above the shell's bottom tabs and wraps; it must not cover the final fields or keyboard focus. From 1280px, retain two centred panes with a wider index and preview line per row. Preserve the same edit and reason across resizing. Disabled sections, warning counts, accordion expansion, pending saves and conflict comparison must be accessible without relying on color or pointer hover.

## 4. Capability accounting

The inventory's current-location rows remain evidence of shipped behavior until implementation. Record this issue under planned ownership; do not mark prototypes as shipped.

| ID | Acceptance / coverage obligation |
| --- | --- |
| LEDG-01 | Replace the single Edit militia ledger toggle with per-section Correct/Cancel; retain a reachable temporary roster/officer editor. Test one local editor and Cancel without a write. |
| LEDG-02 | Values: focus, rank, training, treasury in copper, notoriety. Defaults/validation reuse Setup, intentional numeric overrides remain possible. |
| LEDG-03 | Teams retains manager assign/replace/clear from roster people, names and limit warnings. Temporarily preserve roster inclusion/removal, kind, Hit Dice and six officer-role assignments; final roster/officer owner is Characters & officers. Removing a roster person clears their roles and team managers with named warnings, without deleting the character record. |
| LEDG-04 | Preserve every correctable field in the section table below, including add/remove, conditions, asset delivery/receipt facts and both carried benefit types. Test each section's isolated save and nested sibling preservation. |
| LEDG-05 | Each correction requires entered free text, trimmed nonempty, at most the existing 2,000-character server limit. No Militia preset chips or prefilled reason; blank/whitespace fails inline and in the save summary. |
| LEDG-06 | Merge only the edited section into latest accepted state; latest revision on save; same-section conflict shows theirs/yours and Start again from their values. Pending, failure/retry and unknown-ack behavior cannot overwrite remote changes or duplicate an acknowledged correction. |
| LEDG-07 | Section warnings plus collected save-point warnings are advisory; fields and linked error summary distinguish invalid data. Remove only approved explanatory hints. |
| LEDG-08 | Expose previously hidden week context, carried persistent events, queued effects and one-use bonuses read-only, in Changes through the week. No correction fields for them. |
| LEDG-09 | No militia: show No militia yet. and Set up militia; character CRUD remains usable on Characters & officers. |
| LEDG-10 | Responsive skeleton, accessible Loading militia ledger… status, page failure/Try again and successful recovery inside the shell. |
| LEDG-11 — new, planned | Section index/detail with count/warning indicators, phone single-open rows and desktop previews, including accessible navigation and only one correction open. |
| LEDG-12 — new, planned | Before save, identify all staged choices affected by candidate source changes, with human names/slot positions and reachable phase controls; after save recompute warnings on every device. |
| LEDG-13 — new, planned | Recover from source-correction orphaned references through existing draft edits when a complete valid result is possible, or identity-preserving source restoration through the ordinary correction API; cover multiple orphans, reload and another device. No relaxed validation or new payload. |

Shared IDs, each explicitly retained:

| ID | Militia obligation / owner |
| --- | --- |
| SETUP-02 | Reuse Values editor and structural validation; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-05 | Reuse roster/officer fields for temporary fallback; Setup owns initialization, Characters & officers owns permanent replacement/migration. |
| SETUP-06 | Reuse all team fields/manager choices; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-07 | Reuse full character-condition editor; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-08 | Reuse full settlement editor; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-10 | Reuse all item fields; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-11 | Reuse all cache fields; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-12 | Reuse complete order editor including decimals and receipts; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-13 | Reuse all marketplace fields; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-16 | Reuse carried skill-benefit editor; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-17 | Reuse carried Market Day editor; Setup owns initialization. |
| SETUP-19 | Reuse section-keyed advisory warnings; Setup owns initialization review, this issue correction review. |
| SETUP-20 | Reuse field and reference validation with linked errors; Setup owns initialization, this issue merged-correction validation. |
| NAV-11 | Militia no-militia link opens same-campaign Setup; shell owns routing. |
| NAV-16 | Every old correction operation remains reachable throughout rollout; shell temporary hosting is replaced here. |
| NAV-17 | Consume scoped Militia/Characters/Week routes and context-preserving bookmarks; shell owner. |
| CHAR-01 | Character list remains reachable on Characters & officers, not removed when replacing the old ledger tab; Characters & officers owns it. |
| CHAR-08 | Current character changes update manager options/effects and are never overwritten by a stale correction; Characters & officers owns record updates. |
| CHAR-09 | Retain pre-setup/empty/archive behavior on Characters & officers; shell owns unavailable campaign. |
| WEEK-03 | Repair navigation changes only this player's Phase View; Week frame owns phase navigation. |
| WEEK-08 | Preserve pending-save/Confirmation departure safeguards and recovery feedback when navigating between Militia and Week; Week frame owns weekly barrier. |
| WEEK-12 | Militia links into existing same-campaign week states; Week frame owns those states. |
| STATE-01 | Shell banner leaves militia readable/editable; paused writes fail normally with fields/reason retained. |
| STATE-02 | Militia owns its section skeleton; shell owns name/account skeleton. |
| STATE-03 | Use shell's shared card: The militia could not be loaded. with page-local Try again, tabs usable. |
| STATE-04 | Respect shell organization selection/unavailable state; never show stale prior-organization facts. |
| STATE-05 | Militia owns its loading/failure/no-militia distinction; campaign access remains shell-owned. |
| STATE-06 | Saved corrections, warnings and restored references update other players and survive reload. Shared regression obligation. |
| STATE-07 | Use shell neutral unavailable/sign-in gate before protected page reads. |

**Signed-off replacements/removals:** [separate workflows](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/103#issuecomment-5834024251) replaces LEDG-01's whole-page toggle and `/militia/correct` with in-place corrections and transfers roster/officer ownership; this does not authorize removing that fallback early. [Prototype approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5844235691) removes explanatory captions: the weekly-actions hint, keep-and-explain warning hint, reason helper, “you can still save…” line and conflict explainer. Keep concise warnings, field labels, actionable errors, read-only group label and validation. [State approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381) replaces visible ledger-loading copy with skeleton/accessibility status and pre-setup ledger content with the no-militia page while preserving character access elsewhere. No field, manager operation or reason requirement is removed.

## 5. Data, payloads and rules

**No schema, query/mutation argument, result-shape or Weekly Resolution change; no Ruleset Version increment or database migration.** Reuse `canonicalLedger.read({campaignId, militiaId})` → `{revision, state}`, `canonicalLedger.save({campaignId, militiaId, expectedRevision, snapshot, reason})` → revision, existing authorized character subscriptions and the existing `canonicalDraftPersistence.workspace`/weekly-store source. All server membership/scope and structural/reference checks remain. No new correction-history query or batch-draft operation. Consult `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` before backend work.

Current seams: `use-canonical-ledger.ts`, `canonical-campaign-dashboard.tsx`, `militia-setup/*`, `canonical-setup.ts`, `canonical-weekly-source.ts`, `canonical-roster.ts`, `weekly-draft-references.ts`, `weekly-draft-contract.ts`, existing weekly controller/store; server `canonicalLedger.ts`, `lib/canonicalDraftPersistenceAuthority.ts` and accepted-campaign tests. Keep routes presentational, saves in a service hook, edit orchestration in a controller and merge/reference derivation in pure utilities. Consume [Setup's shared-editor/validation contract](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138): editors bind existing paths, accept authorized choices, preserve raw invalid input, never save independently; derive typed warning section keys locally without changing `prepareMilitiaSetup`'s string result or parsing English message text.

### Exact section projection and merge

| Section | Replace only these snapshot fields | Fields that must stay reachable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Values | `focus`, `rank`, `training`, `treasuryCopper`, `notoriety` | All five values. |
| Teams | `roster.teams` | Add/remove; name, type, active/disabled/missing, reward-cap exemption, manager, notes. Removing a disabled/missing team remains available here after Upkeep's Remove was retired. |
| Settlements | `settlements` | Name, reputation, secured/occupied, temporary shift, Reduce Danger shift/end week, refuge activated/end weeks. |
| Character conditions | `characterActions.people` | Character, available/hidden/captured/recovering/dead, headquarters/refuge/elsewhere and description, PCs must rescue, capture source/week, rescued/restored week. Preserve any sibling state. |
| Items | `economy.items` | Name, value, militia/character owner, identified, weight, location. |
| Caches | `economy.caches` | Location, class, status, secure/extradimensional, return Activity week, item contents. |
| Orders | `economy.orders` | Item/settlement, source/kind, ordered week/day, due day/Activity week, price, delivery days, enchantment value, record/clear receipt and received day. Preserve supported decimal fields. |
| Marketplaces | `economy.markets` | Source/settlement, available/expires week, availability/percent, sale percent, contraband. |
| Carried benefits | `eventBenefits.skills`, `eventBenefits.markets` | Skills: characters, skills, bonus type/value, settlement, after-dark, start/end week. Market Day: settlements/start/end week. Preserve source identities and all supported existing facts. |

Never replace an entire `roster` or `economy` container from the opening form when saving one child section. Preserve absent/optional containers as appropriate and keep entity identities/order stable. `snapshot.characters`, `bonuses`, unrelated siblings and all latest week/context facts remain authoritative. Week & carried effects displays current week/start day, first-week skip, previous-week uneventful carry, last buyoff week, persistent instances with age/order/targets and mitigation facts, queued effects and one-use bonuses. It has no Correct control. Existing read-only carried/order dependencies can forbid removal of an entity: surface that integrity error with the relevant item; advisory open-week warnings do not bypass it.

### Correction lifecycle and concurrency

1. On Correct, capture the accepted section value plus campaign/militia/current-week identity. Local raw values and a blank reason are the edit. Other devices remain free to edit.
2. Derive warnings against the newest source and current open Weekly Draft. At Save compare the latest section to the captured section using stable structural equality (the existing canonical serialization may be reused). A change to the same section, even another row, enters conflict; don't silently field-merge or overwrite it.
3. Show **Another player changed this section**, their latest values beside the player's intended values, and **Start again from their values** plus Cancel. Restart resets the baseline/fields to the newest section, clears the old reason and requires a newly reviewed correction. Do not invent an actor name: the read result has no actor. Preserve both views until the player chooses.
4. If only other sections/character records changed, merge this section onto the latest snapshot, retain all their data, run full structural/cross-reference validation and recompute warnings. Send the latest revision and explicit reason. A team manager removed from the roster meanwhile is a field/reference error, not a silently cleared assignment.
5. A server revision race is not permission to force-save. Refresh/reconcile; if the section changed show conflict, otherwise retain input/reason, rebuild the candidate and let the player retry. A week change requires restarting the correction from the new week's facts; do not apply an old-week edit to a successor automatically.
6. Save shows Saving correction… and prevents duplicates while pending. Success closes the editor and shows current accepted values with accessible feedback; other players' read views/warnings update immediately. Failure keeps input/reason. The API has no correction idempotency key: for an unknown acknowledgement, reconcile latest accepted section/revision before offering another save, never blindly replay a full snapshot or claim a reason was stored without an acknowledged save. Campaign/organization changes must not retarget a delayed write or expose old edit state.

The temporary full roster/officer editor retains its existing revision-bound save behavior, full validation and required reason; it must not run concurrently with a new section editor. Its known full-snapshot stale conflict is not silently converted into a broad merge. Use the production fallback, not prototype character controls. Later Characters & officers consumes this section-conflict/reference utility but owns safe roster-removal cascades across people/officers/managers, then removes the fallback.

### Affected choices and reachable repair

Use `draftReferenceRequirements` with the **candidate corrected snapshot as both source arguments** to detect references removed by a correction; passing the old source as `before` would incorrectly keep deleted identities available. Compare with current requirements to distinguish existing issues. Reuse the helper's handling of entities produced by staged actions and event trees. Map paths to named Activity slot positions, Upkeep decisions/transfers, operating settlement, event targets/checks/Sabotage, Persistent officer selections and Table Adjustments. Show human names when known and contextual missing-entity descriptions otherwise; never expose opaque IDs. Refresh against live choices, not a stale draft captured when Correct opened. Roster membership/condition/manager changes also use existing rules warnings/readiness where the referenced character still exists; do not falsely call removing roster membership deletion of a character record.

Show **This affects the open week** before saving, naming choices and linking to their phase/selection. Offer a reachable route to repair choices before removing the source (Cancel the correction, repair the choices, then reopen it). Warn that affected weekly choices need repair; do not imply unrelated weekly edits will save. The warning remains advisory: a structurally valid correction may still be saved, per approval. A newly staged choice racing after preflight remains possible; recompute after acceptance and on every device.

The existing server rejects **any** draft edit whose resulting **whole draft** has an orphan, with `Invalid draft entity reference`; it also blocks Confirmation. Do not loosen that check, add a multi-edit operation, silently clear choices, auto-apply a Table Adjustment or show a nonexistent successful save. The page and phase selectors must still render missing references and usable recovery controls rather than crash or disable the entire draft.

Concrete recovery using existing contracts:

- When a single existing semantic edit repairs **all** current missing references, offer the existing clear/replace/detail/phase control and check its complete candidate before sending. Keep pending/failure/accepted feedback from the weekly store. Merely clearing one slot while another orphan remains is not sufficient.
- For multiple orphans that no single edit can repair, provide **Restore missing team/settlement/item/cache** entry points in the appropriate ordinary Militia section. This is a UI path to the existing full-snapshot correction, retaining the missing identity from that campaign's current draft rather than allocating a new one. Reuse captured authoritative pre-correction facts when available; otherwise collect required facts in the normal editor, showing which choice needs them. Never fabricate old names/stats, promise historical facts after reload, allow raw-ID entry, or create a character record through this path. Standard structural validation, membership/scope checks, section conflicts and an explicit new correction reason still apply. Restoration merges only that section into the latest source and must not undo unrelated concurrent changes.
- Source restoration does not edit the draft and `canonicalLedger.save` checks carried dependencies rather than all staged choices, so separate valid section restorations can proceed even while other staged orphans remain. Restore prerequisite items before caches when required by snapshot integrity. Once all references exist, repair the staged choices normally, then make the originally intended deletion as a new reviewed correction. Do not silently save that deletion automatically.
- The existing read exposes the open draft's missing identities but no correction archive. After reload or on another member's device, recovery still starts from those identities and explicitly entered current facts; only still-available captured facts may be prefilled. Already re-created identities use the current section instead of producing duplicates. Carried-context failures, missing characters or unrelated corrupt state are not permission to write protected character records or change the API; route character/roster cases to their existing authorized owner and surface a specific error when integrity cannot be restored by a supported operation.

This is client implementation of the approved repair requirement. Current code permits valid same-identity restoration: snapshot schemas check uniqueness/references, and `canonicalLedger.save` has no deleted-entity tombstone restriction; it does protect `snapshot.characters` and carried dependencies. Add a real integration proof below before shipping. Do not substitute a link-only recovery that strands a multiple-orphan draft.

### Validation and later migration

Use react-hook-form + zod, `noValidate`, styled field messages and a linked save summary. Differentiate empty-required values from malformed numbers, preserve supported decimals and don't misalign adjacent controls when an error expands. Full merged-snapshot integrity remains blocking; rule caps/rank/training/manager limits are warnings, without a required acknowledgment or extra note beyond the correction reason. Managers remain roster references; archived assignments remain visible with warnings. Values, conditions and source corrections never resolve a week or change frozen Resolution Records.

At this rollout stage retain today's representable character/roster kinds and officer facts. Do not pre-apply prototype PC/NPC enums, new manager limits or Hit Dice fallback. [Characters & officers authoring](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/132) must update this page's manager options/warnings, roster compatibility, shared editors, Setup/browser envelopes and weekly consumers when its approved migration ships. It owns the next unused Ruleset Version for changed resolution behavior; dropping roster kind is not approved.

## 6. Validation and coverage

Retain equivalent behavior for **every existing `e2e/` scenario**; update navigation/field locators for sections without deleting scenarios, weakening auth or skipping the required-result gates.

| Existing tests | Required equivalent after delivery |
| --- | --- |
| `character-ledger.spec.ts` | Two members share character changes, then assign an officer through the retained correction fallback with a reason; reload preserves assignment. Adapt old Ledger-tab locators only. |
| `existing-militia.spec.ts` | Mid-campaign setup, open Values correction, modify treasury and confirm persistence without losing other imported facts. |
| `canonical-workspace.spec.ts`, `support/setup-workspace.ts` and phase helpers | Setup and shared editor fields/warnings remain intact; phase navigation, draft choices, errors, Table Adjustments, Rules Exceptions and Confirmation remain equivalent. |
| `access.spec.ts`, `support/nightly-flows.ts` | Member versus outsider visibility, character CRUD/edit/reload and campaign/organization separation remain. |
| `realtime-action-slot.spec.ts`, `complete-week.spec.ts`, `canonical-cutover.spec.ts` | Shared Action Slots, accepted corrections/source after reload, normal next week and immutable history remain. |
| `canonical-persistence.spec.ts`, `canonical-confirmation.spec.ts` | Keep direct backend real-auth/isolation, competing writer/stale review, delayed/dropped acknowledgement, rollback and immutable-history contracts. |
| `convex/acceptedCampaign.integration.test.ts` | Existing ledger membership, revision protection, carried-reference rejection and character-edit preservation still pass. |
| `convex/canonicalDraftPersistence.integration.test.ts`, `src/lib/weekly-draft-references` consumers | Whole-draft reference rejection and campaign-scoped references stay enforced; repairs do not weaken them. |
| `src/components/militia-setup/form.test.tsx`, `src/lib/canonical-setup.test.ts` | Shared editors retain required reason, required/invalid numeric errors, defaults, order decimals/receipts and reference validation. |

Add focused pure/controller/component and integration coverage for:

1. Every listed correction section and field, one-open mode, Cancel, empty/whitespace/long reason, invalid data versus advisory warnings, full section error links and manager operations; retain field values across responsive changes.
2. Two players correcting different sections preserve both saves; an Items save preserves concurrent Caches/Orders and Teams preserves roster/roles. Two edits in one section show accurate theirs/yours and require restart. Character update, manager roster removal, revision race, week advancement and scope change during editing cannot be overwritten by a stale snapshot.
3. Named pre-save warnings across all reference families; client-generated Action Slot entities are handled correctly. Protect carried events/orders/queued effects; no “warning” permits a structurally invalid source save. No mutation on warning navigation/Cancel.
4. Integration proof: stage two choices using two removable teams, accept a valid correction removing them, show both affected choices on both devices, refuse an unrelated edit and a one-slot clear while another orphan remains, then restore the exact identities through reasoned section saves, clear/reassign choices through normal operations and successfully apply the intended removal. Also cover mixed item/cache or settlement/Activity+Event references, restoration order, remote recreation/conflict, and reload/second-device restoration with explicit field entry instead of invented archival facts. Confirmation remains blocked until required repairs and usual readiness are complete; no audit/history API added.
5. Read-only carry across remote updates/Confirmation; no editable controls for week or carried instances/queue/bonuses. All saved reasons still reach `canonicalSourceCorrection` without a user-facing correction-history feature.
6. Militia loading, failed/Try again, no-militia→Setup, unavailable/sign-out/wrong organization and maintenance write failure. Pre-setup character creation and roster/officer fallback stay reachable. Phone/tablet/desktop, keyboard focus, accessible warning/conflict/pending states and no controls obscured by the reason bar or bottom navigation.

Run `pnpm -s typecheck`, `pnpm -s lint`, relevant local/component/Convex integration tests and affected required/nightly browser journeys using the existing isolated-preview harness. Report actual executed checks and any live-service limits; unrun live coverage is not a pass. This authoring task does not implement or deploy anything.

## 7. Routes and rollout

Canonical destination is `/campaigns/<id>/militia`. Shell's `/campaigns/<id>/militia/correct` compatibility address redirects here; do not introduce a standalone correction page. Week repair links use `/campaigns/<id>/week?phase=<phase>` and existing local selection/focus behavior; query/hash focus is client navigation, never a new stored draft field. Links retain the campaign and never change another player's Phase View. Characters & officers targets `/campaigns/<id>/characters`; before Setup it remains usable. Militia's empty state links to `/campaigns/<id>/setup` and respects Setup's initial-started page versus live-completion behavior.

Native shipping chain: **[guided Militia Setup](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138) → this issue → Characters & officers**, inside the agreed twelve-area order. Wire the native dependency on Setup, and the downstream issue's dependency here when [Characters & officers authoring](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/132) publishes. Authoring tasks are not runtime blockers. The shell and Week frame contracts already exist; phase owners keep their earlier delivered behavior while this issue adds reference-repair integration.

Keep the shell-hosted full correction editor until all replacement sections work. Then retain a clearly reachable **People & officers** fallback using the existing roster/officer editor, with a link from Characters & officers. It remains mutually exclusive with section editing and retains reasons/validation/stale-save handling. Remove it only after Characters & officers delivers equivalent roster inclusion/removal, officer assign/move/remove, Hit Dice/kind behavior, manager-clearing warnings and realtime/access coverage. Team manager editing remains permanently on Militia Teams; character record CRUD remains on Characters & officers. No prototype merge or premature removal of an old control.

### Published implementation handoffs

Implement after [Implement guided Militia Setup with browser resume](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138). The next shipping area is [Implement Characters & officers with role corrections and compatible kind migration](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141). The native dependencies between implementation issues encode this shipping order; authoring tasks are already complete.

## 8. Shippable when

- All nine correctable sections and the read-only carry view expose every accounted capability at tablet, phone and desktop sizes; only one local correction is open; reasons, validation, warnings and accessible feedback work.
- Latest-section merges preserve concurrent changes and current character facts. Same-section conflict, server race, week change, failure and unknown acknowledgement never blindly overwrite or retarget edits.
- Affected weekly choices are named before save, remain visible afterwards on all devices, and have proven recovery for both single and multiple orphans using unchanged APIs. Reload/second-device recovery requires no nonexistent history source, raw identity entry or fabricated facts.
- Existing roster/officer functionality is still reachable pending its successor; managers remain with teams; shared Setup editors and normal weekly Confirmation/history contracts still work.
- Empty/loading/failure/access/maintenance behavior matches the shell and page decisions, with membership and campaign isolation enforced and no clipped or hidden controls.
- Add the Militia Correction glossary entry; update inventory shipped locations/coverage only after implementation. Required checks and relevant tests pass with actual E2E evidence reported. No unapproved payload/rules change, new correction-history feature or lost capability.
