body:
Implementation parent: [Militia UI rework](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148) · Original planning map: [UI rework decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99) · Authoring task: [Write this area spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/132).

When creating implementation tickets from this spec, follow the [source traceability requirements](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148#source-traceability-and-future-tickets): link back to this spec and carry forward the relevant decision-comment permalinks, amendments, pinned prototypes and capability IDs from the sections below.

## 1. Scope and ownership

Implement **Characters & officers**, position **10 of 12** in the [agreed rollout](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504), at `/campaigns/<id>/characters`. Deliver the six officer cards, character records, roster membership and two separate reasoned correction modes. Own the approved `pc | npc` migration, roster-kind mirroring, role-based manager limits and commandant Hit Dice fallback, including every already-shipped consumer.

[Militia corrections](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139) owns Teams and manager editing, section conflict/reference-repair primitives and other militia sections. [Guided Setup](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138) owns initialization and shared form primitives; this issue updates them for the migration. [Navigation shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135) owns campaign access, routes, account/organization controls and maintenance; [Week frame](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137) owns weekly feedback/readiness. Activity owns staging Change Officer Role: this page shows pending actions but never stages them. No correction-history query, full character builder, new manager editor here, hard deletion or history rewrite.

Acceptance for the page:

- Tablet landscape: Officers header with militia focus, six role cards in a 3×2 board, then one alphabetical character table. Each role remains visible when vacant and shows its rule, current effect, holders, source and relevant pending actions. Characters has Add character, Show archived, Pending this week with Go to Activity, and columns On roster, Character, Kind, Hit Dice, Officer roles, Teams and Edit. Preserve access to six ability scores and notes through the full record dialog.
- Correct officers enables Assign and holder menus in place. Assign lists roster people grouped PC/NPC with the effect each candidate brings compared with the current effect. Move to… replaces that holder's selected role; Remove removes that assignment; Assign can add another role without removing existing ones. No duplicate character/role pair. Chips in character rows navigate/focus the corresponding role card.
- Correct roster enables only On roster and optional Hit Dice override. Joining uses the record's kind without asking again. Leaving removes that person's officer assignments and clears their team managers in the same correction; warn with the affected role and team names before Save. The record, character conditions, items and historical facts remain. Add character is an immediate record operation, followed by explicit roster inclusion as a separate correction.
- One correction is open locally at a time; dim the other correction section. Both support Save/Cancel, one required reason and editable quick-pick reasons: Story change, Fixing a mistake, New officer joined, Character left. This approved exception to Militia's no-preset-reasons pattern applies only here. Save-point warnings, strategist before/after action allowance and conflict presentation sit above the reason. No per-assignment saves or claims/locks.
- Add/Edit uses one dialog for name, PC/NPC, **Hit Dice**, STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIS/CHA and notes; the existing numeric `level` field remains the record storage. An existing record also offers Archive/Un-archive. Archiving never removes roster membership, roles or manager assignments. Show archived reveals archived rows; occupied role cards always retain archived holders and warnings, even when those rows are hidden.
- Hit Dice displays a plain effective value for everyone. Explicit roster `hitDice` overrides the record's `level`; blank means use `level`, including NPCs whose record number is presented as Hit Dice. Do not add a second character-record Hit Dice field or provenance caption. Preserve zero overrides (`??`, not truthiness), existing integer/nonnegative override validation and record number ≥1.
- Show the counting holder and non-stacking message for redundant holders; commandants total distinct holders' effective Hit Dice. Strategist shows “+1 militia action; that action gets +2”; Overseer shows the secondary-check bonus and one-event support. Derive effects from the shared rules utilities, including the best allowed ability and focus, rather than prototype arithmetic. Show concise advisory warnings for multiple roles, archived assignments and manager over-capacity. Assigning a PC includes the approved Change Officer Role/Go to Activity hint.
- “Manages N of M teams” is read-only and links to this campaign's Militia Teams. Pending Change Officer Role facts come reactively from the open Weekly Draft, display both above the table and on affected cards, and remain distinct from accepted assignments. Changes/removals/Confirmation refresh those facts; never apply pending roles early.
- Phone (<768px): two compact role cards across, Assign picker inline below them, and character cards containing all row operations/facts. The reason bar wraps chips and sits above shell bottom navigation, with scroll padding so it obscures nothing. Tablet Assign uses the approved picker sheet. Desktop (≥1280px): centered 3×2 board over table; Assign uses a floating panel. Keep state when resizing and keyboard/focus/accessible labels throughout.
- Load role-card/table skeletons with accessible status; failures use “Characters could not be loaded.” and Try again while tabs stay usable. Without a militia, character CRUD still works and all six cards show “Set up militia to assign officers.” with a same-campaign Setup path. Retain No active characters/No archived characters states. Respect shell sign-in/unavailable gates and readable maintenance banner; attempted paused writes fail normally with input retained.

## 2. Decision sources

The full discussions, not mock behavior, are authoritative:

- [Officer assignment, corrections, manager limits and approved kind/Hit Dice changes](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/112#issuecomment-5836835106), including its earlier roster/removal handoff.
- [Character page variant B, separate corrections and record-owned kind](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/114#issuecomment-5844673552), superseding the earlier character screen.
- [Separate Setup/Correction workflows and reference warnings](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/103#issuecomment-5834024251).
- [Setup/correction prototype and signed-off caption removals](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5844235691); its character strip/combined side sheet is superseded by the character-page decision.
- [Navigation and team-manager ownership addendum](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/102#issuecomment-5831173561).
- [Shared states, pre-setup character access and removal of Select a campaign…](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381).
- [Responsive pages variant C](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/121#issuecomment-5846528685).
- [Rollout, compatibility scope and next-unused Ruleset Version amendment](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504). Its version policy supersedes the officer decision's obsolete literal 4→5 instruction.

Use `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/ai/ironfang-militia/militia-rules.md` and `militia-tables.md` for domain language and baseline mechanics, with the explicitly approved changes above taking precedence. Add the agreed **Officer** glossary entry in implementation: a character holding a militia officer role; an NPC is an Officer exactly while it holds at least one role, independent of its `npc` kind. Role removal changes that status, not the character's kind. Reuse Militia Setup/Militia Correction entries delivered by preceding owners.

## 3. Prototypes

| Branch and pinned commit | Approved route/variant | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`prototype/characters-officers` at `c6f90faecb0109c39f202c89475962e2c0014b31`](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/c6f90faecb0109c39f202c89475962e2c0014b31) | `/prototype/characters-officers?variant=B`, `pnpm prototype` (3017); select “kind lives on the character record” in the scenario panel | Tablet board/table, separate correction modes, role picker, warnings, record dialog; scenario controls exercise concurrent change, pending actions and remote Spymaster. |
| [`prototype/responsive-pages` at `cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c`](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c) | `/prototype/responsive-pages?variant=C&page=characters`, `pnpm prototype` (3013) | Phone/tablet/desktop and loading/failed/empty scenarios. Integrate the actual shell, not its stand-in. |

Prototype branches remain unmerged. Real authorization, records, errors, conflict guards, migration, complete fields and authoritative rules replace mocks. Use the later Hit Dice naming and plain effective values; do not revive the setup-correction prototype's six-column strip or combined side sheet, roster-owned-kind scenario, extra captions or alternate responsive variants.

## 4. Capability accounting

These are **planned** ownership/coverage changes to `docs/ui-capability-inventory.md`; keep existing IDs and current shipped locations until implementation.

| ID | Acceptance/coverage owned here |
| --- | --- |
| CHAR-01 | Character access/counts move from the embedded collapsible ledger to the dedicated page/table; no lost CRUD access before or after Setup. |
| CHAR-02 | Name-sorted active records, kind and effective Hit Dice; all six stats remain readable/editable in the full dialog. |
| CHAR-03 | Add dialog preserves every existing field/default/validation, with approved PC/NPC and Hit Dice labels; reusable by Setup. |
| CHAR-04 | Edit same dialog, immediate shared record update and retained input on failure. |
| CHAR-05 | Archive in record dialog, assignments preserved and warned. |
| CHAR-06 | Show archived on table and Un-archive in dialog; empty archived state. |
| CHAR-07 | Inline create/update/archive errors, pending acknowledgement, retry and retained values. |
| CHAR-08 | Reactive records, kinds, roles, roster, effects and managed counts on all members' devices; reload persistence. |
| CHAR-09 | Page skeleton, failed/Try again, active/archived empty states and pre-setup records; consume shell access gate. |
| LEDG-03 | Own roster membership/Hit Dice and six-role assign/move/remove, atomic role/manager cleanup on roster removal; Militia corrections retains manager editing. |
| CHAR-10 — new | Role board with current/non-stacking/commandant effects, vacancy, source attribution, candidate contributions and strategist allowance preview. |
| CHAR-11 — new | Pending Change Officer Role display and same-campaign Activity links, derived from open draft without staging anything. |
| CHAR-12 — new | Separate Correct officers/Correct roster modes, quick-pick required reasons, roster conflict handling and named cascade warnings. |
| CHAR-13 — new | Per-character role navigation chips and read-only managed-team count/limit links to Militia Teams. |

Shared IDs, with their owners:

| IDs | Obligation here / owner |
| --- | --- |
| LEDG-01, LEDG-05, LEDG-06, LEDG-07 | Consume Militia corrections' one-open/reason/save/conflict/validation primitives for these two corrections; preserve these capabilities when removing its temporary fallback. |
| LEDG-09 | Pre-setup character CRUD remains here; Militia corrections owns its no-militia page. |
| LEDG-12, LEDG-13 | Consume Militia corrections' affected-choice warnings and valid reference-repair paths; own roster/officer restoration and integrity behavior here. |
| SETUP-05, SETUP-06, SETUP-19, SETUP-20, SETUP-24, SETUP-26 | Update Setup roster/officer/manager editors, warnings, validation, browser envelopes and inline record dialog for kind and Hit Dice migration. Setup remains flow owner. |
| ACT-09, ACT-10, ACT-13, ACT-16, ACT-17 | Activity owns slots/details/check displays/exceptions/warnings; this delivery updates their officer, manager-limit and commandant rules consumers and revalidates staged choices. |
| WEEK-02, WEEK-03, WEEK-04, WEEK-05 | Week frame owns phase navigation/readiness, independent Phase Views, shared updates and optimistic previews; changed officer facts/effects propagate without moving another player. |
| SUM-05 | Review & confirm owns stale-review recovery; character/source revision changes invalidate stale Confirmation normally. |
| HIST-04, HIST-05 | Finished weeks owns historical presentation; preserve old version/provenance and recorded outcomes through compatibility readers. |
| NAV-16, NAV-17 | Consume shell section navigation/scoped routes; retire fallback links only after replacement access exists. |
| STATE-01, STATE-02, STATE-03, STATE-04, STATE-05, STATE-06, STATE-07 | Shell owns pause/access/shared failure pattern; own this page's skeleton/error/empty states, write feedback and cross-device persistence. |

Signed-off replacements/removals: [character-page approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/114#issuecomment-5844673552) replaces CHAR-01's embedded collapse, CHAR-02's table arrangement, CHAR-05/06's archive placement and the superseded combined correction screen; all underlying data/actions remain reachable. [Officer approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/112#issuecomment-5836835106) replaces officer_npc/other_npc choices with NPC and removes required commandant override in favor of level fallback. [Caption approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/113#issuecomment-5844235691) removes explanatory subtext, reason/conflict helper paragraphs and keep-and-explain hints; preserve concise warnings/labels and the separately approved PC-to-Activity hint. [State approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381) removes only CHAR-09's Select a campaign… and replaces access-loading text with a skeleton. **No approval to drop roster.kind, archive records automatically, delete stats/notes, remove manager editing or rewrite old records.**

## 5. Data, payloads and rules

Inspected main: `eef41f7bad19e63ecce858e7a4490c937a4ece89`, Ruleset Version 5. Recheck implementation-time main. [Upkeep](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140) ships earlier and owns characterless transfers and compatible dice totals; preserve that contract. Allocate the **next unused Ruleset Version when these changed resolution mechanics ship**, after any earlier rule changes. Do not promise 5, 6 or reuse Upkeep's version. Format/presentation alone needs no bump; manager-limit and commandant behavior does. Client preview and server Confirmation must agree; old Resolution Records keep their exact versions/sources/results.

### Existing API seams and approved changes

Reuse `character.listByCampaign`, `createCharacter`, `updateCharacter`, `archiveCharacter`; `canonicalLedger.read/save`; `canonicalSetup.options/initialize`; current workspace/open-draft reads and weekly edit APIs. Preserve argument/result structure, except the explicitly approved kind-enum change and its compatibility acceptance. `listByCampaign` with `includeInactive` already supplies full authoritative record kind. `canonicalSetup.options.characters` does **not** include kind: compose its existing result with that authorized character read in Setup; do not silently add a result field/query. Do not add kind to `snapshot.characters`, which currently holds rules facts without it. Retain roster.kind as the record mirror.

Relevant seams: `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/character.ts`, `convex/lib/canonicalCharacters.ts`, `convex/canonicalLedger.ts`, `convex/canonicalSetup.ts`; `canonical-roster.ts`, `canonical-setup.ts`, `canonical-weekly-source.ts`, `rules-officers.ts`, `rules-teams.ts`, `team-manager-rules.ts`, Activity/foundation resolution and Confirmation; character-manager, shared Setup editors, correction controller and draft-reference helpers. Read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` and applicable Convex skills before backend work. Keep routes presentational, state transitions in focused controllers, writes in service hooks, and rules/migration transformations pure and shared.

### Compatibility and migration

1. Widen live validators/readers before new writers to accept legacy character `pc | officer_npc` (including absent kind), legacy roster `pc | officer_npc | other_npc`, and new `npc`. Normalize explicit legacy NPC kinds to `npc`; missing record kind follows existing PC default. For an existing mismatch the authoritative record wins when populating the roster mirror; never infer kind from held roles. Do not add/drop memberships or assignments during normalization.
2. Migrate live character rows and live roster mirrors in bounded, resumable/idempotent internal batches. Keep authorization/campaign reference checks on public paths; migration cannot be a public bypass. Update source revision when accepted live source changes so stale reviews/corrections cannot overwrite it. Preserve IDs, order, Hit Dice overrides/nulls, archive flags, notes, stats, teams, current week and open draft contents. Missing/foreign records are integrity errors to diagnose, not permission to manufacture records or discard references.
3. Maintain the mirror atomically in every subsequent character write and live source write. The existing `updateCanonicalCharacter` already refreshes canonical facts and roster kind in the same mutation; extend that seam to the normalized kinds. Setup initialization and correction saves resolve each roster person against the campaign's current record kind before accepting the new live snapshot. Never let a stale Setup/correction payload restore the old kind. Keep stale-reviewed-character checks and exact snapshot-character protection.
4. Old clients/old forms may still submit the former enum during rollout: accept/normalize legacy kinds at the compatible boundary, while new UI only writes PC/NPC. Refresh stale clients safely; don't narrow storage/API readers while old supported writes can produce those values. Separate current-write normalization from historical parsing. Old Resolution Records, source corrections and any immutable archived payloads must stay readable without being rewritten; a blanket enum replacement in shared schemas must not make them fail to parse or transform their stored identity/source key.
5. Migrate already-saved **Setup browser envelopes** after the scoped account/organization/campaign has been authorized and current records loaded. Upgrade envelope version, map legacy values and mirror each selected record's current kind while preserving raw invalid numeric strings, other steps, IDs, initialization attempt identity, selected step/mode and explicit HD overrides. Missing records surface field errors; don't erase them or invent kinds. No automatic submission. Continue existing started-militia cleanup and same-ID/same-source retry safety; if initialization is already accepted, show/enter the accepted militia rather than resubmitting a migrated source.
6. Update all live kind readers and affected rules consumers, including Setup inline CRUD/options composition, shared roster forms, Militia Teams manager choices/warnings, Activity details and Change Officer Role checks, phase modifiers, pending-action displays, Week reference/readiness/preview, server Confirmation and test factories/fixtures. Search all `officer_npc`, `other_npc`, `hitDice`, manager-limit and commandant consumers; retain legacy adapters only where compatibility requires them. Historical displays use recorded results, never new calculations over today's records.

An extra endpoint, wire field, new stored exception marker or dropped roster field is outside approval and requires human sign-off; the paths above require none.

### Rules semantics

Use a single role-aware manager-limit utility: PC → max(1, Charisma modifier); NPC with ≥1 held role → the same; NPC with no held role → 1. Recompute using the roster at the point the rules evaluate that action, including relevant prior changes in the Weekly Draft; do not infer Officer from kind or count merely pending roles as already held on this page. Retain existing manager Charisma contribution to team checks and distinct-person counting. Going over the limit during weekly choices uses Activity's existing reasoned Rules Exception mechanism; Militia Corrections use their one correction reason, display the warning and preserve a quiet warning afterwards, with no new marker. Removing an NPC's last role warns with their new limit and managed count. A roster removal clears all that person's managers, not the teams themselves.

Commandant contribution is each distinct holder's `rosterPerson.hitDice ?? character.level`, summed for successful Drill using existing Drill semantics. Remove the old missing-HD readiness requirement and Setup blocker only for this approved fallback; missing character facts remain blocking integrity problems. Explicit overrides survive character level edits, and clearing the override resumes following the current record number. Non-stacking roles, one-event Overseer support and strategist +1/+2 rules remain as before. Rule warnings are advisory; structural/reference errors remain blocking.

### Correction projection, races and reference repair

Use existing `canonicalLedger.save` with a latest complete snapshot, expected revision and trimmed reason (nonempty, max 2,000). No new correction idempotency token or draft edit is introduced.

- At open, capture campaign/militia/week and roster baseline. These modes depend on roster people, officer assignments and team-manager edges, so compare the roster baseline to the latest roster before saving; a remote roster change enters the approved conflict flow rather than overwriting related assignments. Changes only to other snapshot sections are merged from the latest source. Character facts always come from the latest source; refreshed stats recalculate visible effects/warnings, while a kind mirror update counts as a roster change.
- Officer mode replaces only `roster.officers`. Roster mode replaces membership/overrides in `roster.people`, removes officer entries for people actually removed, and clears **only** team manager references to those people using the latest teams. Preserve every other team field and unaffected assignment. Mirror kind from current records, preserve `snapshot.characters` verbatim, and never replace a whole old snapshot/container.
- Conflict shows “Another player changed this section”, theirs/yours and Start again from their values/Cancel; restarting takes the latest baseline, clears the prior reason and requires review again. A revision race refreshes/reconciles; if roster is unchanged keep input/reason and offer retry against a rebuilt latest candidate, otherwise conflict. A week change restarts from new-week facts. Delayed work cannot target a newly selected campaign/organization.
- Named pre-save warnings include removed roles/managers, lowered capacity/strategist allowance, affected selections/required officer choices and existing/new draft-reference problems. Reuse Militia corrections' helper with candidate snapshot as both source arguments; don't claim roster removal deletes the character record or always creates an orphan. Pending Change Officer Role or an Overseer selection can become semantically invalid even while its character still exists. Link the affected Activity slot/phase using existing local focus behavior.
- Corrections may save with advisory open-week warnings. Recompute on all devices afterward. Whole-draft missing-reference checks still reject edits whose complete result remains invalid; no silently clearing staged actions, multi-edit API or relaxed server checks. A single existing edit can repair only when its whole candidate is valid. Otherwise use the predecessor's identity-preserving restoration flow. Here a removed roster person can be re-included from its existing character record through a new reasoned roster correction, followed by an officer correction if needed; then repair weekly choices normally. Missing/foreign character records cannot be fabricated via source restoration, and archive/un-archive retains identity. Preserve carried-context restrictions and identify a specific integrity failure if no supported repair exists.
- Saving feedback prevents duplicate submissions; success acknowledges acceptance and closes the mode, failure retains fields/reason. An unknown acknowledgement reconciles latest state/revision before any retry; without an acknowledged response don't claim a reason was stored or blindly replay a full snapshot. Record CRUD remains immediate and reactive through existing APIs; no new CAS contract is invented for the character dialog.

Use react-hook-form/zod, `noValidate`, field-local required-versus-format messages and a linked save summary. Preserve raw input and do not misalign neighboring controls when messages grow. No extra acknowledgment checkbox or exception note beyond the required correction reason.

## 6. Validation and coverage

Retain equivalent behavior for **every existing `e2e/` scenario**; change locators/navigation, never delete coverage because controls moved. Relevant anchors:

| Existing suites | Required equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e/character-ledger.spec.ts` | Two members share creation/stats; include record through Correct roster, assign officer through Correct officers with reasons, observe remote updates and reload persistence. |
| `e2e/access.spec.ts`, `e2e/support/nightly-flows.ts` | Full character create/edit/validation/reload and membership/organization/campaign separation. |
| `e2e/existing-militia.spec.ts`, `canonical-workspace.spec.ts`, `support/setup-workspace.ts` | Complete New/mid-campaign Setup, roster/roles/managers, all migration-affected fields, shared editors, phase readiness and warnings. |
| `e2e/realtime-action-slot.spec.ts`, `complete-week.spec.ts`, `canonical-cutover.spec.ts` | Action Slots, officer/manager effects and accepted source still persist; complete Confirmation advances normally. |
| `e2e/canonical-persistence.spec.ts`, `canonical-confirmation.spec.ts` | Real-auth isolation, stale review, competing writes, delayed/dropped acknowledgement, atomic rollback, next-draft identity and immutable history. |
| `src/components/character-manager.test.tsx`, shared Setup form tests, `canonical-setup.test.ts`, `canonical-roster.test.ts` | Full CRUD/archive/errors/defaults and normalized kind, override/fallback, membership, validation and warning behavior. |
| `rules-foundations.test.ts`, `rules-activity.test.ts`, `foundation-acceptance.test.ts`, `team-manager-rules.test.ts`, weekly resolution tests | New role-based capacities and distinct commandant fallback/override arithmetic, unchanged non-stacking/strategist/Overseer/Drill outcomes, correct new Ruleset Version. |
| `convex/acceptedCampaign.integration.test.ts`, `canonicalSetup.integration.test.ts`, draft persistence/Confirmation integration suites | Atomic record/mirror updates, current source revision safety, authoritative kinds, scoped refs and no record rewrite. |

Add focused coverage for:

1. All six vacant/filled roles, candidate contributions, assign/move/remove/add-second-role, duplicate-pair prevention, effect source and non-stacking ties, archived holders, pending Action Slots and role-chip focus. A tied role must not display stacked contribution. This page never mutates Action Slots.
2. Roster join/leave and optional override, named multi-team/role cascades, cancel without writes, one correction mode, reason chips and required/long reasons. Different unrelated sections preserve both saves; concurrent roster/officer/team-manager edits conflict rather than losing assignments; stats updates recalculate and kind changes invalidate the baseline. Week advance, scope switch, failure and unknown acknowledgement remain safe.
3. PC and NPC with/without roles at positive/zero/negative Charisma; last-role removal and role addition alter limits correctly; over-limit correction allowed with warning/reason, weekly exception required through the existing mechanism. Successful/failed/natural-one Drill, multiple commandants, blank versus zero versus explicit override, level changes and archived commandants agree between preview/server.
4. Migration fixtures for both legacy NPC labels, absent record kind, mismatched mirrors, archived characters, partial/repeated batches and in-flight old payloads. Prove no lost IDs/assignments/raw Setup input; authorized saved Setup envelope restores with new kinds and old invalid fields repairable. Options result stays unchanged. Character kind updates atomically update source/mirror and reject stale reviewed saves; foreign IDs and ordinary outsiders remain denied.
5. Old records containing legacy enums/null HD and earlier Ruleset Versions still parse/display their recorded source/results unchanged; new records use the new version/rules. Preserve Upkeep's old/new roll compatibility and characterless transfers; don't reintroduce officer restrictions or recompute historical outcomes.
6. Affected-choice warnings and repair for pending officer choices, lowered strategist allowance, removed managers and multiple-reference failures. Integrate the Militia corrections restore/repair proof; valid source corrections don't imply an unrelated invalid draft edit can save. Reload/another device can restore membership using the existing record without invented archival facts.
7. Pre-setup CRUD, no active/archived records, load/retry, shell unavailable/sign-out/wrong organization, maintenance failures, keyboard/focus and phone/tablet/desktop. Record form fields, reason bar and pickers remain usable with long names and errors. Remote changes refresh all boards, manager links and weekly effects.

Run `pnpm -s typecheck`, `pnpm -s lint`, relevant unit/component/Convex integration tests and affected required/nightly E2E using the existing isolated-preview harness. Preserve required-result gates and report actual execution and live-service limits. This authoring task implements/deploys nothing.

## 7. Routes and rollout

Ship after [in-place Militia corrections](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139), before Finished weeks, with native implementation dependencies in the agreed twelve-area chain. Authoring-task dependencies do not substitute for shipping dependencies. The earlier [Setup](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138), [Week frame](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137), [Upkeep](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140) and Activity outputs remain shippable as this migration updates their consumers.

Use `/campaigns/<id>/characters`; Go to Activity uses `/campaigns/<id>/week?phase=activity`, manager links target `/campaigns/<id>/militia` and open Teams locally, Setup uses `/campaigns/<id>/setup`. Keep shell's `/canonical-*` redirects, campaign/phase context and browser navigation; do not add a standalone `/militia/correct` screen or reveal internal versions/IDs in copy. Legacy fallback links now point at the replacement page only once all replacement operations work.

Keep the predecessor's **People & officers** fallback until roster inclusion/removal, all officer operations, Hit Dice, archive warnings, kind migration, reasons/conflicts, manager-clearing warnings and real-time/access coverage exist here. Then remove that temporary editor and link, preserving Teams' permanent manager editor and all other Militia corrections. Sequence compatibility readers before writers and finish the live-data/browser migration without narrowing historical readers. Prototype code is never merged wholesale.

### Published implementation handoffs

Implement after [Implement in-place Militia corrections and reference repair](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139). The next shipping area is [Implement Finished weeks with immutable records and paged audit history](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/146). The native dependencies between implementation issues encode this shipping order; authoring tasks are already complete.

## 8. Shippable when

- Board/table, separate corrections and full record dialogs work at all three breakpoints, including every capability above, non-stacking/source effects, pending Activity links and pre-setup CRUD.
- Roster membership/roles/managers remain internally consistent; latest-source merges, required reasons, conflicts, affected-choice warnings and proven repair cannot silently discard another player's edits or staged choices.
- PC/NPC record authority and retained roster mirror hold for all writes, migrated live data and resumed browser Setup; old supported inputs/readers remain compatible. No unapproved schema/result/endpoint change.
- All affected Setup, Militia, Activity and weekly consumers use the same role-based limits and commandant fallback. Preview/Confirmation agree, next unused Ruleset Version is allocated once, and historical payloads/outcomes remain untouched.
- Shared state/access/maintenance behavior is preserved, the temporary editor is removed only after equivalence, Officer is added to the glossary, inventory shipped locations/coverage are updated and required checks/tests pass with actual evidence recorded.

body:
Implementation parent: [Militia UI rework](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148) · Original planning map: [UI rework decisions](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99) · Authoring task: [Write this area spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/133).

When creating implementation tickets from this spec, follow the [source traceability requirements](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/148#source-traceability-and-future-tickets): link back to this spec and carry forward the relevant decision-comment permalinks, amendments, pinned prototypes and capability IDs from the sections below.

## 1. Scope and ownership

Deliver **Finished weeks, rollout position 11 of 12**, after [Characters & officers](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141), before Campaign list/home. This implementation issue is outside the [UI planning map](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99), authored by [Write the Finished weeks implementation spec](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/133). Application main inspected: `eef41f7bad19e63ecce858e7a4490c937a4ece89`; the inventory authoring branch describes planned behavior, not shipped code.

Own the finished-week list, latest/default and explicit week selection, previous/next navigation, five-entry audit paging, record dates, historical integration of the six-section presentation, read-only notices and page states. Own the approved new listing query, which Campaign home reuses for its latest-three preview. Do not implement Historical Correction, Historical Reconstruction or a History Rewrite editor, a correction-note field, historical recalculation or a new rules engine.

[Review & confirm](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/145) owns the pure shared six-section presentation contract; this issue owns the frozen-record adapter integration and its historical compatibility tests. [Navigation shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135) owns campaign-scoped routes, access/organization boundaries, shell navigation, shared failed-load presentation and maintenance banner. [Week frame](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137) owns week/history reference links and the cross-device confirmed-week notice. [Upkeep](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140) owns old/new roll and transfer compatibility; [Event](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/143) owns its versioned occurrence behavior; [Persistent](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/144) owns its live-only recorded-buyoff-warning removal; [Characters & officers](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141) owns kind/Hit Dice compatibility. Consume those contracts without rewriting stored records.

### Page acceptance

- Tablet landscape: an oldest-first week index on the left, selected record on the right. Open the latest finished week by default, visibly selected at the bottom. Each row shows week number, effective record date, up to two truthful headline changes, and corrected/entry-count or reconstructed marker as applicable. End with **Week N is in progress** using the actual open week, not highest historical week plus one. Gaps and mid-campaign starts remain valid. The latest row replaces the standalone Latest finished week button.
- Previous/next arrows in the record header navigate actual recorded week numbers, skipping gaps; disable the unavailable direction. Selecting a different week selects its effective record and resets that week's audit page/disclosure and Show all state. Return to this campaign's current week stays reachable.
- Header: week, provenance, selected record date and recorded Ruleset Version. When an older record is selected, show **Earlier entry X of N** using that record's zero-based sequence plus one and the effective chain's entry count. The complete detail always belongs to that selected record; the index continues to summarize each week's effective record. No context chips under the header.
- Show **N entries** only for multiple entries. It expands an inline newest-first page of at most five audit entries, each with Entry N, provenance, its date, its recorded Ruleset Version, selected state and effective marker. **Earlier entries** loads the next page of up to five, preserving the selected record. Do not append pages into an unbounded visible list. Keep a route back to the first audit page/effective entry: reopening the disclosure resets to the newest page without changing the selected record; selecting the effective week row also resets selection. No correction notes.
- Detail has exactly **1 Upkeep, 2 Activity, 3 Event, 4 Persistent, 5 Table Adjustments, 6 Result · week N+1 began**. Sections stay expanded. Phase headers show recorded net changes; ordered consequences show recorded checks and effects. Rules Exceptions, warnings and recorded outcomes appear under their items; detached facts are preserved through the shared contract. Same-week persistent decisions and reactive Sabotage stay with their Event source, while carried-event decisions stay in Persistent. Nothing is double-counted.
- Table Adjustments retain their original order, effect, kind and quoted reason. With none: **No Table Adjustments. The Final outcome equals the Rules Baseline.** History has no reason fields, add/edit/remove/reorder controls, obsolete-exception removal or Confirm controls.
- Result columns are **Value / At confirmation / Rules Baseline / Final**. Default to facts changed between source/baseline or baseline/final, including changes reversed by an adjustment. Final differences use text as well as color. **Show all values** reveals every recorded value, roster/officers, recorded Operating from, uneventful carry, first-Upkeep skip and the successor context. Context is not deleted when moved here. Treasury display uses copper-exact gp formatting.
- One footer line replaces the two old notices: **Read-only. Recorded when the week was confirmed. Corrections to a finished week aren't available yet.** Retain the prominent provenance label for reconstructed/corrected entries; never imply an earlier audit entry is effective.

## 2. Decision sources

Read the complete discussions, including amendments; these named links own the design decisions.

- [Finished weeks: Ledger variant A, oldest-first and context under Show all](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/117#issuecomment-5845007868).
- [Authoritative Finished weeks amendment: new query, creation dates, five-entry paging and no correction notes](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/117#issuecomment-5845032926). This overrides the original claim that all audit entries show at once and no payload changes are needed.
- [Summary's six-section rules-order presentation](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/110#issuecomment-5844063536), implemented by [Review & confirm's pure live/frozen boundary](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/145).
- [Shared loading, unavailable, failure, empty and maintenance states](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381).
- [Responsive pages, variant C](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/121#issuecomment-5846528685).
- [Campaign home's recent finished weeks](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/118#issuecomment-5846080538), with [rollout/query ownership](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504) superseding its suggestion to fetch recent weeks through repeated detail reads.
- [Twelve-spec template, compatible gradual rollout and completion gate](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504).

Use `CONTEXT.md` terminology and the existing historical immutability contract. Rule numbers remain in the canonical code and `docs/ai/ironfang-militia/{militia-rules,militia-tables}.md`; this issue only presents stored outcomes.

## 3. Prototypes

| Reference | Approved variant and route | Pinned commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Finished weeks](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/2e9904c8afae05107a9f10ff7eb6112beea6ee7a), `prototype/finished-weeks` | A, Ledger; `/prototype/finished-weeks?variant=A` | `2e9904c8afae05107a9f10ff7eb6112beea6ee7a` |
| [Responsive pages](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c), `prototype/responsive-pages` | C, Stacked; `/prototype/responsive-pages?variant=C`, select history | `cf13bfc6c852fc897ef39459ca6cc53b45fc243c` |
| [Summary](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/tree/65d472dcf4bb65094efb97b621c7bbae3ee18965), `prototype/summary` | B; `/prototype/summary?variant=B` | `65d472dcf4bb65094efb97b621c7bbae3ee18965` |

Keep these branches unmerged. Finished weeks B/C and responsive A/B are alternatives, not requirements. The approved amendment is authoritative even where the pinned mock still maps all entries and gives Earlier entries no real paging handler. Implement actual capped paging, real dates, record-only facts, truthful legacy fallbacks, membership checks and empty/error states. Do not ship mock fixtures/state toggles, hardcoded weeks or a correction-note field. Preserve current theme/fonts, use shadcn/ui and focused controller hooks; page components remain thin, pure derivation stays outside views, and derived selection/render data does not require Effects.

## 4. Capability accounting

All entries below are **planned**, not shipped. Preserve the inventory's stable IDs and record actual locations/tests only when implementation lands.

| ID | Owned acceptance and coverage |
| --- | --- |
| HIST-01 | Latest effective week defaults; oldest-first index visibly selects its latest row. Test no explicit selection, reload and sparse recorded weeks. |
| HIST-02 | Previous/next skip gaps, boundaries disable correctly; latest is reachable through bottom row; local selection and browser navigation preserve campaign. |
| HIST-03 | Whole-record audit selection, effective/earlier labels, Entry N, max five entries, Earlier entries and return to effective; no merging audit records or correction notes. Test more than ten entries. |
| HIST-04 | Selected week's header/provenance/date/Ruleset Version, effective/earlier status and merged read-only footer; test dates belong to the selected document. |
| HIST-05 | All existing recorded choices/context, source militia, baseline/final plans, warnings/exceptions/adjustments/outcomes, final outcome and successor facts remain readable in the six-section/Show all layout. Test missing-source and legacy artifacts. |
| HIST-06 | Old History correction card is merged into the footer; corrections-unavailable information stays visible to every organization member. |
| HIST-07 | Page-shaped loading, shared Try again error, no-finished-week CTA and neutral shell unavailable/sign-in state. |
| HIST-08 — new, planned | Approved finished-week listing and direct selection of any recorded week, with effective-record date/headlines/provenance/entry count. Bounded query/list paging also supplies Campaign home's latest-three preview. |

| Shared ID | Boundary and coverage |
| --- | --- |
| NAV-10 | Shell and Week frame own entry links; Finished weeks resolves their requested campaign/week correctly, including confirmed-week notice links. |
| NAV-11 | Shell/Setup own destination; history's no-militia empty state retains Set up militia. |
| NAV-12 | Finished weeks owns final Return to current week CTA; shell's Week tab also retains access. Both keep campaign scope. |
| NAV-17 | Shell owns scoped routes/legacy redirects; history preserves supported week/recordId/beforeSequence selectors through direct links, reload and Back/Forward. |
| WEEK-19 | Frame owns cross-device Week N confirmed notice; this page opens the linked just-confirmed immutable record. |
| SUM-06 | Review & confirm owns shared comparison; history integrates At confirmation/Baseline/Final and complete Show all. |
| SUM-07 | Review & confirm owns live exception editing; history presents every recorded reason/obsolete exception without editing controls. |
| SUM-08 | Review & confirm owns adjustment mutation controls; history preserves ordered effects, kinds and reasons read-only. |
| SUM-10 | Review & confirm owns shared ordered consequence renderer; history supplies only selected-record consequences/checks. |
| SUM-11 | Review & confirm owns shared item placement; history preserves all selected-record outcomes, including orphaned subjects. |
| STATE-01 | Shell owns maintenance banner; finished weeks stays readable throughout the pause. |
| STATE-02 | Shell renders immediately; history owns responsive index/detail skeleton and Loading history screen-reader status. |
| STATE-03 | Shell owns failed-card pattern; history owns failure/retry for list, selected detail and audit metadata. |
| STATE-04 | Shell owns active-organization/sign-in/no-access boundary; historical data cannot cross it. |
| STATE-05 | History owns page loading/failure/empty; campaign unavailable is shell-owned. |
| STATE-06 | Shared subscriptions/reload retain accepted records and selected audit facts; local selection on one device never changes another's selection. |

**Signed-off replacements/removals:** [Finished weeks approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/117#issuecomment-5845007868) replaces HIST-02's Latest button with the latest list row, HIST-03's always-visible Show effective record/entry controls with the entries disclosure, HIST-04's context chips with Show all, HIST-05's ten collapsible containers with six expanded sections and complete comparison/context, and HIST-06's separate notice with the merged footer. These are presentation replacements, not loss of recorded facts. Its [amendment](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/117#issuecomment-5845032926) explicitly **retains HIST-03 Earlier entries** and omits correction notes; no paging removal is authorized. [Shared state approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/119#issuecomment-5846266381) replaces HIST-07 loading/error/empty wording and Reload history with accessible skeleton/Try again/empty CTAs. [Responsive approval](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/121#issuecomment-5846528685) changes layout only. Existing Rules Exceptions and Table Adjustment reasons are not correction notes and remain visible.

## 5. Data, payloads and rules

### Approved boundary and current implementation

Only the approved new finished-week listing query and **record creation dates in query results** ship here. No storage/schema change, new history mutation, correction notes, history rewrite, Weekly Resolution change or Ruleset Version bump. Keep all old Resolution Record payloads byte-for-byte unchanged. Do not add timestamps inside `CanonicalResolutionRecord`; use query envelope metadata from Convex document `_creationTime`.

Current seams: `convex/canonicalHistory.ts`, `convex/lib/canonicalDraftStorage.ts`, `convex/lib/canonicalStorageValidators.ts`, `src/lib/canonical-resolution-record.ts`, `src/components/historical-week/{screen,record-view,record-facts}.tsx`, plus the shared presentation introduced by Review & confirm. Read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` and the Convex skill before backend edits. Use object-form functions with argument/return validators.

Current `canonicalHistory.read` already accepts campaignId, optional week, recordId and beforeSequence; it returns one selected record, effective ID, adjacent recorded weeks and up to five audit entries. Audit entries currently contain only recordId, sequence and provenance. The existing index `by_campaignId_and_week_and_sequence` supports effective tips, sparse adjacent weeks and bounded chain paging. `by_recordId` supports scoped selected-document lookup. Append-only storage requires each new sequence to supersede the previous effective tip and increments sequence from zero: **effective sequence + 1 is the entry count**; selected sequence + 1 is Entry N. Do not count by collecting every correction.

### One shared listing query

Add `canonicalHistory.list` with:

- `campaignId: Id<'campaign'>` required; optional nonnegative integer `beforeWeek` (exclusive descending week boundary), optional integer `limit` (default 25, 1–50), optional nonnegative integer `selectedWeek`.
- Result `{ weeks, earlierWeek, selected }`: `weeks` contains at most limit distinct finished weeks in descending week-number order; `earlierWeek` is the oldest returned week when another older week exists, otherwise null, to pass as the next beforeWeek; `selected` is that exact selectedWeek's effective row or null. Without selectedWeek it is null. It is independent of the list window, allowing a deep-linked older record to get accurate entry-count/header metadata without loading every intervening week. If selectedWeek is already in weeks, reuse that same row.
- Each row is `{ week, effectiveRecordId, effectiveSequence, entryCount, provenance, rulesetVersion, createdAt, headlineFacts }`. `createdAt` is the effective document's `_creationTime`, an epoch-millisecond instant; provenance/ruleset come from that same effective record. No duplicate row for each audit entry. A corrected row's date is the effective record's creation date, not a fabricated original Confirmation date. Corrected marker uses entryCount > 1; an uncorrected reconstruction uses its actual provenance.
- `headlineFacts` is **at most two compact comparison facts**, each `{ key, label, before, final, beforeRecorded, finalRecorded, unit }`; before/final are scalar string/number/boolean/null values, unit is `number | gp | text`. Key is an internal stable semantic key, never displayed. Treasury values remain integer copper when unit is gp. Null and recorded flags distinguish an absent entity/value from an unavailable legacy fact. Label uses record-local names or stable numbered fallbacks only.
- Select headline candidates deterministically from supported stored before/final facts: treasury, training, rank, notoriety, focus, team additions/removals/conditions, settlement reputation, then persistent-event changes, with stable recorded ordering within each family. Include only genuine known changes, not today's rules predictions; extract current artifact facts from stored source/plan-before and finalOutcome/plan-after, retaining supported legacy extraction. The client formats signed deltas, changed text or added/removed subjects from these pairs. If the record lacks comparable facts, headlineFacts is empty and the client shows **Recorded outcome available**; do not assert No changes or calculate a delta from missing zero. Full facts stay available through the selected-record reader.
- Do not return full source choices, snapshots, plans, raw records or all corrections merely to draw two headlines. This query exposes only the compact projected comparisons and metadata above. Projection reads the effective record; it does not call a rules resolver or fetch today's labels.

Implementation uses bounded index seeks: find newest effective tip below beforeWeek, then repeatedly seek strictly below the returned week for the next tip. Each seek skips that week's entire correction chain; do not scan a page of raw audit documents and mistakenly treat it as a page of weeks. Fetch one additional tip for the older-page indicator. selectedWeek uses an exact-week indexed descending first query. Validate every returned tip against the authorized campaign/militia scope. No unbounded collect, count scan or added table/index is needed.

History loads the newest page, sorts its rows ascending for the approved oldest-first index, and prepends older pages on **Earlier weeks** at the top. All finished weeks remain reachable; every displayed segment is oldest-first, and latest stays the bottom row. This bounded loading control is an implementation detail for the newly approved list, distinct from the fixed five-entry **Earlier entries** audit control. On direct links outside the loaded window, render selected metadata/detail immediately and load the relevant index window without sequentially fetching every intervening page; gaps and omitted pages must never be presented as absent records. Keep the cached newest row visible at the bottom as the Latest finished week selection; it restores the newest index window. Mark omitted ranges with a load-more control rather than inventing missing weeks. Merge repeated/reactive rows by week, using effective ID/sequence to update a row rather than duplicate it. A new effective entry refreshes its summary; selected earlier record detail stays pinned.

Campaign home calls **this same query with `{ campaignId, limit: 3 }`**, no beforeWeek or selectedWeek. It receives the three greatest recorded week numbers, in latest-first order, metadata for Corrected/From setup badges and dates, and the same optional headline pairs. Zero, one or two rows are valid. It never requests three full records or adds a second listing endpoint. Campaign home owns preview wording/layout/links; this owner supplies the tested contract. Week frame can reuse it after this rollout but its earlier delivery cannot depend on it.

### Date-only extension of the existing reader and bounded audit metadata

Retain every existing read argument and result member. Add top-level **`createdAt`** for the selected record document, and **`createdAt`** to each existing audit row. When recordId selects an older entry, its date comes from that older document, not the effective row. Preserve scoped lookup rejection for missing/foreign/cross-week records. No date field is written or backfilled in storage. Format consistently with a semantic `<time dateTime=...>` and a readable localized date; no query-side wall-clock dependence, invented in-game date or fake timestamp.

The approved audit display needs a Ruleset Version, but dates-only approval does **not** authorize silently adding `audit.rulesetVersion` or changing audit paging. Fetch a missing visible entry's stored version through the existing `canonicalHistory.read({ campaignId, week, recordId })` contract, reading `record.rulesetVersion`; reuse selected/effective reads already available. Keep these reads restricted to the currently expanded maximum-five-entry page and unsubscribe/discard stale requests when the page/campaign changes. They are audit-detail reads, not the listing query or Campaign home's latest-three implementation. Metadata load/failure stays local to that entry and can retry; do not substitute the effective/current Ruleset Version. Keep a readable loading status until complete, with no wrong entry flash. Audit dates/provenance/selection already come from the main page's result.

Use selected-row listing metadata to obtain the total/effective sequence; derive selected Entry N from the matching audit entry when available. For a direct recordId not on the visible audit page, locate its ordinal by bounded existing five-entry page reads, stopping on that ID and cancelling on selection/scope change. Do not add an unapproved read metadata field or fetch the entire audit chain at once. While locating, show **Earlier entry** without fabricating X; the selected immutable detail may already display. Every audit selection stores its known sequence locally; reload can resolve it again. An invalid recordId is unavailable, never silently replaced with a different entry.

### Scope, selection and states

Both queries derive identity server-side, require organization membership and verify campaign/militia association before returning any facts. Retain the current `requireScope` contract; new listing uses the same authorization, not a caller-supplied user/organization identity. No GM role distinction. Shell checks campaign membership in the active organization's campaign list and presents neutral no-access/not-found; backend remains authoritative even when called directly. Record IDs must belong to the requested campaign, militia and week. beforeWeek/selectedWeek/limit and existing numeric selectors reject malformed, fractional, negative or out-of-range inputs as appropriate.

Current history read throws when no militia exists. Preserve that API behavior; page/home first use the existing shell/setup/workspace context to know whether there is a militia, then skip historical reads when none and show the approved empty state. New listing likewise requires authorized militia scope; do not invent a campaign query or treat no-access as a successful empty history. Current open-week metadata may drive only navigation/empty-state/in-progress copy, never fill a record fact. It must not block already available historical detail if the live week is temporarily loading or failed.

Selection is local navigation state. Explicit week/recordId links stay pinned across new confirmations or corrections; an omitted week follows latest until the user selects a week. Without explicit recordId, that week's effective record may update reactively; with one, the selected immutable record remains unchanged, though its effective/earlier marker and total may change. Switching weeks clears recordId/beforeSequence. Paging changes beforeSequence without changing the selected record; remember its ID when needed so effective-tip changes cannot replace a deliberately selected entry. Audit visibility and Show all are local only. Key controller/subscriptions by campaign/selection so late results cannot flash the previous campaign or overwrite a new selection.

Loading shows a history-shaped skeleton and **Loading history…** status within the shell. Failure uses **Finished weeks could not be loaded.** and **Try again**, preserving usable shell/tabs; list/audit-only failures keep an already selected immutable detail readable with a local retry. Empty authorized history says **No finished weeks yet.** with **Open week N**, or **Set up militia** without a militia. A selected nonexistent week has a selection-unavailable state with access to the finished-week list/latest; do not claim the campaign has no finished weeks. Bad/foreign selectors expose no record facts. Maintenance remains a shell banner and does not remove history reads.

### Frozen-record presentation and compatibility

Integrate Review & confirm's pure contract with **only the selected CanonicalResolutionRecord**: source, optional sourceMilitiaSnapshot, baselinePlan, finalPlan, finalOutcome, adjudication, warnings and successorContext. Query dates/sequence/provenance wrap the header; they cannot change the record's facts. Do not mix an earlier record's source with the effective record's final outcome. No live draft store, mutation callbacks, current-rule invocation, current officer/character lookup or snapshot reconstruction is allowed inside the historical adapter/renderer.

Retain exact recorded artifact formatVersion/rulesetVersion handling and legacy/general fact fallback. Missing source snapshots show **Not recorded** or **Militia facts were not included in this record**; absence is not zero or unchanged. Preserve all supported facts from the union of source, baseline, final and successor, including additions/removals and nonnumeric values: rank/training/treasury/notoriety/focus, teams/conditions/managers, settlements/reputation, roster/officers/characters, bonuses, assets/economy/delivery, carried events/ages/order, queued effects/orders and first-week/carry context. Any legacy fact not expressible as a rich consequence remains in a labelled read-only fallback within the appropriate section/Show all, rather than being dropped. Recorded choices/checks must remain available even when no numerical effect resulted.

Map item attachments through known recorded subject/code conventions and execution provenance, including nested Roll Twice, reactions/Sabotage, persistent decisions and missing subjects. Do not fuzzy-match warning text or collapse identical messages on distinct subjects. Unassociated facts stay in their known phase; if phase is unknown, retain a labelled unassociated-facts group inside the six-section presentation. Phase totals exclude subsequent Table Adjustments; do not replay arithmetic on top of stored final values.

Support Upkeep's legacy dice arrays and new dice totals, legacy transfer actors and new characterless transfers, old/new Event trees, old pc/npc enums/nullable Hit Dice and each recorded Ruleset Version. Display stored reasons/outcomes unchanged. Persistent's removed live recorded-buyoff field/warning does **not** remove historical source amounts or warnings; history must retain them. Later corrections to today's militia, renamed/archived/deleted characters and new rule versions cannot change an old selected record's numbers, names or recorded decisions. Where recorded names are absent, preserve distinguishable numbered labels without exposing opaque IDs.

## 6. Validation and coverage

Keep every existing E2E scenario with equivalent semantics; replace only obsolete layout selectors and signed-off copy.

| Existing coverage | Required treatment |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e/complete-week.spec.ts` | Preserve real Confirmation, next-week arrival, reload and link to immutable history; use scoped route/new Week heading. |
| `e2e/canonical-confirmation.spec.ts` history portion | Rewrite Week N · History, collapsible Rules baseline plan, Final outcome and separate History correction selectors to the six-section Result/Show all/merged footer. Retain both members' history access, no editing/Confirm controls, recorded seven-copper adjustment reason/result (exact gp formatting), stable original result after live treasury changes, independent selection, return to current week and phone/tablet geometry/screenshots. Add desktop. |
| `convex/canonicalHistory.integration.test.ts` | Extend `[rules.P86.history]`, `[rules.P86.authority]`, `[rules.P86.navigation]`: effective-chain count, scoped timestamps, five-entry paging, sparse weeks, old record immutability and all member/outsider/cross-campaign/cross-week checks. |
| `src/components/historical-week/screen.test.tsx` | Rewrite `[rules.P86.controls]` for list/header arrows/disclosure, paged selection and merged footer while retaining effective-entry recovery. |
| `src/components/historical-week/record-view.test.tsx` | Retain `[rules.P86.display]`/`[rules.P86.labels]` and extend the shared frozen fixtures to prove complete facts and record-local labels with no editor. |
| `e2e/canonical-cutover.spec.ts` | Unchanged immutable record equality after accepted campaign reload and rejection of retired backend paths. |
| `e2e/canonical-persistence.spec.ts`, remaining `canonical-confirmation.spec.ts`, shared persistence/Confirmation contract suites | Retain membership/campaign isolation, stale review, competing writes, atomic rollback, idempotent replay/dropped acknowledgements, closed-draft delayed edits, one successor and exact source/baseline/final/context persistence. Presentation cannot weaken these contracts. |
| `access.spec.ts`, `existing-militia.spec.ts`, workspace and relevant character/action scenarios | Keep the shell/organization, correction/reload and cross-device scenarios reachable; do not delete unrelated cases when changing history selectors. |

Meaningful new tests:

1. Listing with zero/one/three/many sparse weeks, multiple corrections, reconstructions, >50 total weeks, bounded distinct-week paging and selectedWeek outside window. Assert no duplicates/loss, correct latest-three despite gaps/many entries, ascending UI, descending home contract, exact chain counts and dates, compact headline fields, unknown legacy comparisons and no full raw artifacts in results. Prove newest-tip retrieval skips corrections rather than exhausting a raw-record limit.
2. More than ten audit entries: only five visible, multiple Earlier entries requests, terminal page, reopen-to-newest, effective recovery and earlier entry direct URL/reload. Verify dates and Ruleset Versions per actual entry; cap active metadata readers to five, handle one failed metadata load, cancel late results and keep detail/entry identity unchanged during paging. No correction notes or newly widened read metadata.
3. Two authorized members choose different weeks/entries independently; new Confirmation appears in both lists and home latest-three data, omitted selection follows latest, explicit selection stays pinned, and a newly effective correction changes the marker/summary without altering selected historical facts. Switch campaign/organization mid-load, revoke access and retry without leaking cached content.
4. Six sections and complete Show all with normal/legacy artifacts, absent source snapshot, unnamed distinct characters, zero effects, added/removed facts, baseline change reversed in Final, all four adjustment kinds/order, nested Event/Sabotage/Persistent facts, obsolete/missing-subject exceptions, warnings with duplicate text and unmapped codes, recorded outcomes and next-week context. Changing current live facts/resolver version cannot change the adapter output; spy/assert no mutation/live query/current resolver from the historical renderer.
5. Loading/failed/empty/no-militia, invalid URL numbers, nonexistent week, missing/foreign record, signed-out/outsider/wrong active organization, maintenance, Try again, Return to current week, legacy redirects and Back/Forward. Validate backend directly as well as through shell.
6. Phone 390×844, tablet landscape 1194×834, desktop 1440×900: oldest-first list/one expanded phone row, effective/earlier selection, five-entry paging, wrapped long names/reasons, stacked labelled Result, keyboard/focus, no horizontal overflow or bottom-bar obstruction, same available facts/actions at each width.

Run `pnpm -s typecheck`, `pnpm -s lint`, targeted historical/query/shared-presentation tests and relevant real-auth browser suites before implementation completion. Record actual command/results and environment limitations; an unrun browser test is not a pass. This authoring task does not deploy or execute feature implementation.

## 7. Routes and rollout

Destination `/campaigns/<id>/history?week=<n>`; omitted week selects latest. Preserve existing supported `recordId` and `beforeSequence` query selection through shell routes, reload and browser navigation. Positive/nonnegative interpretation follows existing week validators (week zero is supported by current history tests). Malformed selectors cannot crash the shell. Record selection never changes a shared draft or another player's Phase View.

Keep shell's `/canonical-history?campaign=X&week=...&recordId=...&beforeSequence=...` redirect to the same campaign/scoped selection. Return to current week goes to `/campaigns/<id>/week`; no militia goes to `/campaigns/<id>/setup`. Frame's confirmation link and home rows target the recorded week explicitly. Remove old page-local navigation only when the replacement retains all supported selection/paging capabilities.

Native implementation dependency is **Characters & officers → Finished weeks → Campaign list/home**, following the twelve-area shipping chain. This issue also consumes the already-shipped Review & confirm contract; authoring-task dependencies are not shipping dependencies. Retain the current history browser, query, frozen parsers and legacy compatibility until replacement list, audit, all record sections and responsive states are covered. Add the new query/date envelopes compatibly before switching the view; retain unchanged record payloads and existing reader arguments. Update generated types through the repository's legitimate workflow when implementing, without hand-editing them. No database migration or rules version allocation is required.

The Campaign home authoring/implementation owner consumes the exact list signature/metadata above and owns preview layout/badges/links. Do not add another listing endpoint or pull Campaign home's description/date/create changes into this slice.

### Published implementation handoffs

Implement after [Implement Characters & officers with role corrections and compatible kind migration](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141). The next shipping area is [Implement the Campaign list and home with scoped creation and editing](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/147). The native dependencies between implementation issues encode this shipping order; authoring tasks are already complete.

## 8. Shippable when

- HIST-01 through HIST-08 and every shared obligation above have implemented coverage or their linked signed-off presentation replacement. Inventory preserves IDs/removal history and records actual locations/test evidence only after delivery.
- Oldest-first selection, latest default, gap-aware arrows, effective/earlier whole-record selection, five-entry paging, stored dates and Ruleset Versions work on direct links, reload and browser navigation. Every finished week remains reachable without an unbounded database read; Campaign home's latest-three consumer uses the single list API contract.
- Historical facts come exclusively from the selected immutable record. Complete old/new and missing-source records remain readable, including historical buyoff warnings, choice details, legacy transfers/rolls/kinds, reasons and next-week facts. No raw technical identifiers, invented zeroes or current-rule reconstruction appear.
- Tablet retains index/detail; phone below 768px is one scrolling oldest-first list with only one expanded week, whose detail includes audit toggle and all six sections; desktop from 1280px retains two panes with a wider preview index and centred max-width page. Use stacked labelled Result values on narrow screens, wrapping headers/reasons and shell bottom-tab clearance. These non-week pages follow responsive-pages C, not the Week frame's desktop three-column/no-page-scroll rule.
- Semantic navigation, accessible Previous/Next names, `aria-expanded`/selected states, visible focus, keyboard operation and loading/error status announcements work. Changing week brings the selected heading into view without stealing focus on every remote update; color is never the only selection/warning/difference signal.
- Shell access/maintenance and page loading/retry/empty states remain usable; organization membership and every campaign/week/record reference are tested directly. No history editing, correction notes, schema mutation or Ruleset Version bump is introduced.
- Required checks and meaningful unit/integration/real-auth browser coverage pass with recorded evidence. Existing Confirmation/persistence coverage remains intact and prototype branches remain unmerged.
